nodes.label: Native App contract (app_api.h)
nodes.rationale: Put the app in src/apps/, implement the App contract from app_api.h, register it, and the drawer picks it up. Four rules, each learned the hard way: create on entry, destroy on exit — no app keeps a screen alive in the background; never touch the clock's objects — the host mediates; decor() every decorative object or it breaks the host's gestures (D014); only draw from the LVGL task (D018).

nodes.label: An app platform, and a timer — v1.11.0
nodes.norm_label: an app platform, and a timer — v1.11.0
nodes.rationale: app_api.h — a five-field App contract: name, icon, create, destroy, tick. app_host.cpp — registry, drawer, launch, route home; knows nothing about what any app draws and no app knows anything about the clock. Adding an app is one file plus one line in app_registry.cpp. The timer reuses the same cards and 210 px digits — a second visual language on one device would be one too many. The swipe-up gesture begins as a press, so displacement disqualifies a press whatever its duration (otherwise an upward drag would also fire a tap or a long press); it must start within 80 px of the bottom edge (D027). Found while linking: `const App app_timer = {...}` had internal linkage — a const object at namespace scope is TU-local in C++, so the registry could not see it; extern on the definition is required.

nodes.label: Back is a system gesture and means back — v1.13.0 / v1.15.0
nodes.norm_label: back is a system gesture and means back — v1.13.0 / v1.15.0
nodes.rationale: The left-edge swipe is polled from the LVGL loop rather than handled as a screen event, because LVGL 8 does not bubble events and every clickable child would have eaten the press; polling puts it above the widget tree, where a system gesture belongs — apps get it for free and none can break it (D029). Armed by where it starts (44 px of the left edge), judged on release (110 px rightward, 90 px vertical wander) — the same shape as the clock's swipe-up. The app gets first refusal via an optional App::back(), which Settings uses to close its text editor so a stray edge swipe cannot discard a hand-typed Wi-Fi password. v1.15.0: navigation is a stack — app → drawer → clock — and app_host_back() is the one door for the edge swipe, the timer's back card, Settings' Back and the drawer's Clock button; the drawer is rebuilt on every visit by the same build_drawer() swipe-up uses — nothing resident, PSRAM flat (D033).

nodes.norm_label: back inside a lua app rebooted the device — v1.20.3

nodes.label: POST /launch endpoint
nodes.rationale: Every screen could only be reached by touching it, so every UI change ended with a checklist handed to the owner; that stopped being tolerable when launching a Lua app rebooted the device and the trigger was out of reach. POST /launch {name} opens any screen ('clock' routes home, 'drawer' opens the drawer, any app name launches it). The request is recorded by the web server's task and served on the LVGL loop by app_host_tick(), so the one rule this firmware never broke (D018) still holds. Anyone on the LAN can change what the device shows: same posture as the rest of the API (D034).

nodes.label: A binding may request a lifecycle change, never perform one
nodes.norm_label: a binding may request a lifecycle change, never perform one
nodes.rationale: l_back() ran inside lua_pcall on state L and called app_host_back(), which called running->destroy() = script_destroy() = lua_close(L); lua_pcall then returned into a state that no longer existed. The interpreter was being closed by code it was running. Now l_back() calls app_host_request_back(), which sets a flag the host serves from app_host_tick() on the next LVGL pass, when the Lua call stack is empty. The same deferral POST /launch used to cross a task boundary now crosses a call-stack boundary; one mechanism, serve_pending(), serves both. Anything that destroys the app (back, exit, launching another app) must go through app_host_request_*. Native apps do not need this: their back buttons are plain C++ callbacks and LVGL handles deleting an object mid-event via _lv_event_mark_deleted().

nodes.label: Every native app lays itself out for both shapes
nodes.norm_label: every native app lays itself out for both shapes
nodes.rationale: D043's borrowed landscape was honest scaffolding (apps turned sideways in portrait). Each native app reads lv_disp_get_hor_res/ver_res at create: Timer stacks its cards like the portrait clock; Settings' tabview and keyboard go percentage-sized; the Lab's absolute grids became wrapping flex rows so a future pin wraps instead of clipping; Messages was born both-shaped, its list just gets taller.

nodes.label: Landscape = macOS sidebar, portrait = iOS list-push
nodes.norm_label: landscape = macos sidebar, portrait = ios list-push
nodes.rationale: Settings used an lv_tabview with six tab buttons across the top and horizontally swiped pages; the owner asked for vertical everything, copying Apple. Apple ships two layouts for the same content, chosen by shape, so: landscape (600x450) is a 190 px sidebar of six icon+name rows beside the section's page; portrait (450x600) is the full-width section list with chevrons, each tapping to push the page full-screen. The tabview is gone; section pages are the same six flex columns, only the container plumbing changed. The back stack gained one level and the chip and edge swipe walk it identically: editor -> page (portrait) -> unsaved-changes guard -> host. No horizontal gesture remains in Settings, so nothing competes with the left-edge back swipe (D029), a conflict the tabview always had. Fixed 560-px children (Wi-Fi and city lists) went percentage-width. A seventh section fits without redesign.

nodes.rationale: l_back() called app_host_back() which reached script_destroy() and lua_close(L): the interpreter was closed by the code it was running and lua_pcall returned into freed memory. /launch already deferred across a task boundary; this defers across a call-stack boundary; one serve_pending() does both.

nodes.label: Battery chip and the inverted isBatteryConnect() — v1.21.0 / v1.21.1
nodes.norm_label: battery chip and the inverted isbatteryconnect() — v1.21.0 / v1.21.1
nodes.rationale: 46×22 battery glyph top right, percentage inside, hidden when no battery is connected and in line mode; the SY6970 has no fuel gauge, so percent is a piecewise resting-curve estimate from cell voltage (D042). Polled every 30 s from the loop task because the PMU shares the internal I2C bus with touch, so the bus keeps a single master. v1.21.1: the chip vanished when USB was unplugged — the board's isBatteryConnect() is implemented as getVbusVoltage() != 0 (the real SY6970 detect is error('Not implemented') in XPowersLib), so 'battery present' meant 'USB plugged in'. Presence is now judged from cell voltage (2800–4400 mV, debounced over two reads). Telemetry, not power management: no low-battery shutdown, no deep sleep.

nodes.label: Brightness follows the sun — v1.10.0
nodes.rationale: Settings ▸ Screen ▸ Dim by sunrise: on uses sunrise/sunset from the internet, off uses the fixed night window; default on. The fixed window was wrong every morning between sunrise and the window's end — caught at 06:10 with sunrise at 05:58 and the panel still at night brightness because the window ran to 07:00; the schedule did what it was told and was simply wrong about the world. Open-Meteo already supplies is_day for the weather icon, derived from sunrise/sunset at the exact coordinates, so this costs nothing, tracks the seasons and follows the city. The hour window remains the fallback whenever weather has never arrived. /health reports brightness {day, night, follows_sun}.

nodes.label: Messages: gadgets talk over HTTP and mDNS — v1.24.0 / v1.25.0
nodes.norm_label: messages: gadgets talk over http and mdns — v1.24.0 / v1.25.0
nodes.rationale: Identity is the device name; peers are one mDNS browse away (_gadget-msg._tcp); delivery is POST /msg into the server every device already runs; arrivals announce themselves on the line display and land in a 16-deep inbox; GET /messages and POST /send make the loop drivable from a shell. ESP-NOW and MQTT considered and rejected for cause (D046). v1.25.0: a messenger UI — thread of bubbles, contact book learned from scans, sends and source IPs, an envelope badge on the clock that yields to line mode like the battery chip (D047). Release-discipline note: the first push of Messages went out without the version bump — only the git hash in /health told the truth; FW_GIT existing is what made the slip visible.

nodes.label: OTA updates (POST /update, tools/ota) — v1.16.0
nodes.rationale: POST /update takes a raw firmware image and writes it to the inactive OTA slot; tools/ota builds, pushes, and refuses to call it done until /health reports the new version. No repartition was needed — default_16MB.csv has carried ota_0, ota_1 and otadata since Stage 0, which is why this is a MINOR release and settings survive. Raw body, not multipart, so Update.begin() gets the exact size and the ESP32 magic-byte check rejects a wrong file in the first chunk. Reboot on client disconnect so the 200 provably reaches the caller. The device narrates its own update (flashing / error on the line). Deliberately absent: authentication (private LAN; header-token hook noted), rollback (stock Arduino core cannot — the cable remains the rescue path), resume. v1.16.1 exists only to be the first release delivered over the air.

nodes.label: v1.0.0 — first tagged release
nodes.rationale: Feature-complete against the original brief: Fliqlo split-flap on true black, 600×450, purpose-generated 210 px tabular digit font, two-phase fold on minute change, NTP with POSIX timezone; Open-Meteo weather on a dedicated FreeRTOS task with backoff and stale marker, never on the render path; line display of 32 states in Russell's circumplex reachable over HTTP, BLE NUS and a BLE HID output report; on-device Settings persisted to NVS; custom vendor HID identity; brightness schedule, ±2 px burn-in walk. Measured: cold boot to correct local time 4.45 s against a 10 s budget; emotion auto-revert 5.2 s; malformed API input returns 4xx with no reboot.

nodes.label: Weather glyphs drawn with primitives; a moon after dark — v1.7.0 / v1.8.0
nodes.norm_label: weather glyphs drawn with primitives; a moon after dark — v1.7.0 / v1.8.0
nodes.rationale: Eight icons — clear, partly cloudy, overcast, fog, drizzle, rain, snow, thunderstorm — folded from Open-Meteo's 28 WMO 4677 codes; severity dropped deliberately because at 40 px 'light drizzle' and 'dense drizzle' are indistinguishable and a glance only needs the kind. Drawn with primitives, not bitmaps: eight bitmaps would be ~13 KB of flash, and drawing them means they inherit the palette and stay crisp at any size. memset left the code at 0 (WMO 'clear sky'), so a sun showed before the first fetch — now −1 = unreported. v1.8.0: clear-sky icons follow the sun via Open-Meteo's is_day, so the device never does solar geometry; only clear and partly cloudy change — a cloud looks the same after dark. The crescent is carved by drawing the card colour back over an offset disc, which only works because the icon sits inside a card of known colour. Size hierarchy: temperature and humidity at 44 px (live readings), min/max smaller (a forecast you consult) and moved inside the temperature card in v1.7.3 as context for the headline figure.

nodes.label: Lua app script contract
nodes.rationale: A script is /apps/<name>.lua in LittleFS implementing on_create, on_tick, on_back, on_exit as globals, with bindings ui, gpio, millis, log, back; it appears in the drawer beside native apps with no reboot (tools/app add|list|rm). Uploads are compiled on the device, so a syntax error is rejected with the parser's message and any working version of that name survives. Upload as application/octet-stream: ESPAsyncWebServer parses a text/plain body containing '=' as form data and never calls the body handler, so Lua source (full of '=') arrives empty with no error anywhere.

nodes.label: Launching a Lua app rebooted the device — v1.20.1
nodes.norm_label: launching a lua app rebooted the device — v1.20.1
nodes.rationale: luaconf.h tests LUA_USE_C89 with defined(), so the library's -DLUA_USE_C89=0 — added to 'be explicit' — switched C89 mode ON for lib/lua only (library.json flags do not reach the consumer): lua_Integer was 4 bytes inside the library and 8 in src/script.cpp, so luaL_checkversion correctly reported different numeric types. The error was raised inside luaL_requiref, outside any pcall, where Lua's only option is abort() — so ANY unprotected Lua API error rebooted the device, in a runtime whose promise was that a broken script fails alone. lua_atpanic now longjmps back into script_create, which shows the message and closes the state.

nodes.label: Lua 5.4 runtime beside the native apps — v1.19.0
nodes.norm_label: lua 5.4 runtime beside the native apps — v1.19.0
nodes.rationale: Lua 5.4.7 vendored in lib/lua (+148 KB flash, +1 KB RAM). A fresh lua_State per launch, closed on exit — create on entry, destroy on exit holds for scripts as for native apps. Lua allocates from PSRAM, never the internal heap the display driver needs. An instruction budget stops runaway scripts: scripts run on the LVGL task, so `while true do end` would otherwise freeze the clock with the cable as the only way out. Compiled at upload, not launch. io, os, package and debug are not loaded; GPIO bindings enforce the Lab's pin rules. No reboot is needed to see a new tile because the drawer is rebuilt on every visit (D033).

nodes.label: Route: embedded scripting runtime
nodes.rationale: Done — v1.19.0, D037. Lua 5.4, apps as text files, no reboot. Embed a small interpreter and expose the platform as its API — cards, digit fonts, the fold, tick(), back(), HTTP fetch, NVS; the interpreter mediates every call so a broken script fails alone — the sandboxing the hardware cannot provide, provided by construction. Costs known up front: the binding layer is the real work (weeks, not days); one UI thread means scripts stay cooperative; the /update-style upload endpoint and OTA are the delivery path already built.

nodes.label: Scripting runtime candidates: Berry, Lua, MicroPython
nodes.norm_label: scripting runtime candidates: berry, lua, micropython
nodes.rationale: Assessed order of preference: Berry — built for exactly this (Tasmota's app language), ~300 KB, embeds into an Arduino C++ firmware without ceremony; Lua — same shape, larger ecosystem, slightly bigger; MicroPython — official LVGL bindings but heavyweight, and grafting it into an existing Arduino firmware is a rebase, not an addition. Lua was what shipped (v1.19.0).

nodes.label: Compile at upload, not at launch
nodes.norm_label: compile at upload, not at launch
nodes.rationale: script_save() parses into a throwaway state before writing; a broken script is rejected with the parser's own message and the previous working version of that name is untouched, rather than becoming a tile that fails when tapped.

nodes.label: lua_atpanic longjmp guard around script init
nodes.norm_label: lua_atpanic longjmp guard around script init
nodes.rationale: The version error was raised inside luaL_requiref, which script_create calls directly, not under lua_pcall. luaD_throw with no error handler and no panic function calls abort(), which on an ESP32 is a panic and a reboot, so any Lua API error anywhere outside a pcall took the device down. lua_atpanic now installs a handler that records the message and longjmps back into script_create (a panic function must not return); requiref, register_api, loadbuffer and on_create all run inside that guard. On a panic the message is shown on the app's own screen and the state is closed, since a panicked lua_State is unusable.

nodes.label: -DLUA_USE_C89=0 turned C89 mode on
nodes.rationale: lib/lua/library.json carried -DLUA_32BITS=0 and -DLUA_USE_C89=0 to be explicit, but luaconf.h value-tests LUA_32BITS and existence-tests LUA_USE_C89, so =0 enabled C89 mode for the library only (library.json flags do not reach the consumer). lua_Integer became long (4 bytes) inside lib/lua and stayed long long (8) in src/script.cpp; LUAL_NUMSIZES disagreed and luaL_checkversion, reached through luaL_newlib inside register_api, reported 'core and library have different numeric types'. nodes.rationale: Never touches an LVGL object; the LVGL loop polls net_weather(). Keeps rendering unblocked and avoids the classic "LVGL called from two tasks" crash. Sleeps in 250 ms slices so "fetch now" from Settings is honoured promptly.

nodes.label: Async handler -> LVGL is a threading boundary: validate, parse, post to a queue
nodes.norm_label: async handler -> lvgl is a threading boundary: validate, parse, post to a queue
nodes.rationale: ESPAsyncWebServer callbacks run on the async TCP task and must not touch LVGL objects; the LVGL loop picks the request up. Same discipline as the weather task.

nodes.label: BLE unverifiable from the sandbox: macOS TCC kills CoreBluetooth access with SIGABRT (exit 134)
nodes.norm_label: ble unverifiable from the sandbox: macos tcc kills corebluetooth access with sigabrt (exit 134)
nodes.rationale: Denied by killing rather than erroring; the BLE path must be exercised from the owner's own Terminal, which prompts for permission.

nodes.label: Validation: malformed JSON, unknown state, over-long message -> clean 4xx; duration_s clamped
nodes.norm_label: validation: malformed json, unknown state, over-long message -> clean 4xx; duration_s clamped
nodes.rationale: A clean 4xx rather than a reboot; the clamp means a typo cannot hide the clock for an hour.

nodes.label: state "clear" (none/stop/idle) reverts immediately; short 15-30 s durations refreshed while working
nodes.norm_label: state "clear" (none/stop/idle) reverts immediately; short 15-30 s durations refreshed while working
nodes.rationale: 90-180 s durations stranded an animation on a clock nobody could read when a session was abandoned; the device must self-recover within half a minute if Claude goes quiet.

nodes.label: Brightness follows Open-Meteo is_day (Settings > Screen > Dim by sunrise), hour window as the fallback
nodes.norm_label: brightness follows open-meteo is_day (settings > screen > dim by sunrise), hour window as the fallback
nodes.rationale: A fixed 21:00-07:00 window is wrong every morning between sunrise and its end and drifts across the year; is_day is already fetched for the icon, tracks seasons and follows the city.

nodes.label: A duration is how long until the next refresh, not how long to be visible: default 30 s
nodes.norm_label: a duration is how long until the next refresh, not how long to be visible: default 30 s
nodes.rationale: Because every work command is prefixed, each command refreshes the timer; the duration only has to outlive the gap between commands, and what the owner sees idle is the tail after the last push. Removing hush and raising durations to 90-180 s had been an over-correction.

nodes.label: flipclock made global: ~/.local/bin/flipclock + ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md
nodes.rationale: Memory is per-project and tools/say was a relative path, so other sessions never lit the panel. Found while building it: flipclock.local takes the full 2 s timeout from a cold shell while the LAN IP answers in 45 ms (IP first, mDNS fallback, cached host), and backgrounding curl killed the request. Fire-and-forget and silent are not the same property.

nodes.label: flipclock MCP bridge (~/.local/share/flipclock-mcp/server.py): flipclock_say and flipclock_status over stdio, stdlib only
nodes.norm_label: flipclock mcp bridge (~/.local/share/flipclock-mcp/server.py): flipclock_say and flipclock_status over stdio, stdlib only
nodes.rationale: The Chat app has no shell and the clock sits at an RFC1918 address Anthropic's servers cannot route to; MCP servers run as local processes that can reach the LAN. Three rounds were spent fixing better versions of the wrong problem because "outside this conversation" was inferred rather than established.

nodes.label: Humidity at the existing 28 px size, receding by luminance (#4E4E4E vs #8A8A8A); missing value renders nothing, not 0%
nodes.norm_label: humidity at the existing 28 px size, receding by luminance (#4e4e4e vs #8a8a8a); missing value renders nothing, not 0%
nodes.rationale: The two-size budget was spent; a third size starts the slide toward a dashboard. A wrong reading is worse than an absent one.

nodes.label: LVGL 8 alignment is a persistent style property: lv_obj_set_pos on an aligned object is an offset from the alignment point
nodes.norm_label: lvgl 8 alignment is a persistent style property: lv_obj_set_pos on an aligned object is an offset from the alignment point
nodes.rationale: lv_keyboard_constructor aligns BOTTOM_MID, so set_pos(kb, 0, 162) shoved the keyboard 162 px below the screen. Align, never set_pos, for self-aligning widgets.

nodes.label: Caption renders state + message (limit 20 -> 48 chars, wraps to two lines); message is an object, never a verb
nodes.norm_label: caption renders state + message (limit 20 -> 48 chars, wraps to two lines); message is an object, never a verb
nodes.rationale: The caption carried the object while the verb lived in the line's motion, which only helps if you can read amplitude; "reading reading" makes the mistake self-evident. Filenames, concepts, restatements and jokes had been four registers with no rule.

nodes.label: Detect the upload port by USB ID 303A:1001, never by name
nodes.norm_label: detect the upload port by usb id 303a:1001, never by name
nodes.rationale: macOS names the port after the physical socket: /dev/cu.usbmodem2101 became usbmodem1101 when the cable moved and the upload failed with a bare Error 2.

nodes.label: Weather row hierarchy: temperature + humidity at 44 px, min/max at 22 px inside the temperature card (icon 40 deg 31/41)
nodes.norm_label: weather row hierarchy: temperature + humidity at 44 px, min/max at 22 px inside the temperature card (icon 40 deg 31/41)
nodes.rationale: All three at 44 px made the least important value the widest; "on the same pallet as" meant the same frame, not the same palette, and the card measures itself from both labels.

nodes.label: Weather icons drawn with primitives; WMO 4677 folded to eight kinds; is_day -> moon for clear sky
nodes.norm_label: weather icons drawn with primitives; wmo 4677 folded to eight kinds; is_day -> moon for clear sky
nodes.rationale: Eight bitmaps would cost ~13 KB and a second visual language; primitives inherit the palette and stay crisp. Severity is discarded because at 40 px light and dense drizzle are indistinguishable. wx.code initialised to -1 since WMO 0 is clear sky. The crescent is carved by drawing the card colour over an offset disc, which only works inside a card of known colour.

nodes.label: Identity = the device name; _gadget-msg._tcp with name=<identity> in TXT
nodes.norm_label: identity = the device name; _gadget-msg._tcp with name=<identity> in txt
nodes.rationale: One name (Settings > BLE > name) for BLE and messaging; two clocks on one LAN must be named apart because the name IS the address label. Peers are found with one mDNS browse; no pairing, no registry. One mDNS hostname (flipclock.local) remains: the service browse dedupes by name, but a second device should also get a distinct hostname; noted, not built.

nodes.label: Messaging worker task with a command queue; the web task only calls msg_store()
nodes.norm_label: messaging worker task with a command queue; the web task only calls msg_store()
nodes.rationale: Scans and sends block for seconds, so they run on a worker task with a command queue; the UI requests and polls. The web task only ever calls msg_store(), which locks against the readers.

nodes.label: Contact book learns name->address three ways
nodes.norm_label: contact book learns name->address three ways
nodes.rationale: The recipient field takes a contact name or a dotted-quad IP. The book learns (1) from an mDNS scan merging every advertising gadget, (2) from sending to a typed name/IP, and (3) from receiving, which remembers the sender against the connection's source IP, so replying never needs a scan; this is the load-bearing design. A typed name no scan or message has resolved cannot be sent to; the app says so and suggests Scan or an IP. Names are labels; the IP is the address (D046).
nodes.source_file: docs/decisions/D047 - Messages are conversations, and the clock wears the badge.md

nodes.label: Conversations, not an inbox
nodes.rationale: v1.24.0's flat inbox with a peer dropdown was nothing like how anyone reads messages; the owner asked for the phone shape. History entries carry a peer and a direction; the app is a chats list (peer, preview, age) and a thread of bubbles, theirs left in charcoal, ours right in dark green, capped at 3/4 screen width. In-app navigation stacks under the host's back: composer -> thread -> list -> the host pops the app, driven by the same back() hook that saves Settings' passwords. Sent bubbles appear instantly (msg_note_sent writes history before the worker delivers); a failed delivery reports under the thread rather than un-sending the bubble. History is 32 entries in RAM per D046's ephemera stance; LittleFS is there the moment that stops feeling right.
nodes.source_file: docs/decisions/D047 - Messages are conversations, and the clock wears the badge.md

nodes.label: Unread badge pill on the clock, tappable
nodes.norm_label: unread badge pill on the clock, tappable
nodes.rationale: A pill with an envelope, top-left of the clock (the battery chip's opposite corner), hidden at zero and hidden in line mode under the same discipline as the battery chip, and tappable: it opens Messages through app_host_request_open(), the same door the HTTP API uses. Unread clears on opening the app and stays cleared while you are looking at it.

nodes.label: Device gestures
nodes.rationale: Tap: date + weather sync age for 5 s. Long press ≥ 1.2 s: cycle brightness. Swipe up from the bottom edge: app drawer. Swipe in from the left edge, or tap an app's back chip: back one level (app → drawer → clock). Press BOOT on the back: cycle orientation 90° per press. Every screen's back button is the same chip bottom-left (D045). Long-press a drawer tile to move it one place left; the order persists.

nodes.label: Flip 180 is rotation 2, the other landscape (v1.9.0 addendum)
nodes.norm_label: flip 180 is rotation 2, the other landscape (v1.9.0 addendum)
nodes.rationale: Superseded in part at v1.9.0: the owner wanted the panel upside down, so setRotation() IS called now — with rotation 2, the other landscape orientation. Same 600×450, and the library re-applies the CST226SE swap/mirror alongside it, so touch follows the screen with no work here. Exposed as Settings ▸ Screen ▸ Flip 180. The original finding is why this was one line: landscape is native, so flipping is a choice between two landscape rotations rather than a re-layout.

nodes.label: decor() — strip CLICKABLE, SCROLLABLE and SCROLL_CHAIN from anything purely visual
nodes.norm_label: decor() — strip clickable, scrollable and scroll_chain from anything purely visual
nodes.rationale: static void decor(lv_obj_t *o) { lv_obj_remove_style_all(o); clear CLICKABLE; clear SCROLLABLE; clear SCROLL_CHAIN; } applied at all nine decorative call sites in ui.cpp; the layout root alone re-adds CLICKABLE. The rule going forward: decor() is the default for any lv_obj_create() that exists to be looked at; reach for a bare lv_obj_create + lv_obj_remove_style_all only when the object is genuinely meant to receive input — emotion overlays and every app must follow it or they break the host's gestures the moment they appear. (Because it strips SCROLL_CHAIN, drawer tile cells passed through it could not scroll — v1.29.1.)

nodes.label: POST /rotate {deg: 0|90|180|270} (same path as the BOOT button)
nodes.norm_label: post /rotate {deg: 0|90|180|270} (same path as the boot button)

nodes.label: The drawer scrolls again — decor() strips SCROLL_CHAIN — v1.29.1
nodes.norm_label: the drawer scrolls again — decor() strips scroll_chain — v1.29.1
nodes.rationale: The drawer always had a vertical scroller, but the tile CELLS went through decor(), which strips SCROLL_CHAIN — so a drag starting on a tile (99 % of the surface) died at the cell, and scrolling only worked from the 22 px gaps between tiles. Landscape never noticed because its two rows fit; portrait's third row (Trackpad, and any script) was unreachable. Cells now keep the chain, and the drawer's height is computed from the live display instead of a landscape constant.

nodes.label: Every shape, one chrome — v1.24.0
nodes.rationale: Native apps are orientation-native: the Timer stacks its cards in portrait, Settings and the Lab reflow (fixed grids became wrapping flex), and D043's borrowed-landscape now applies only to scripts that have not tagged portrait_ok in their first line; scripts get SCREEN_W/SCREEN_H to branch on. One back chip everywhere: bottom-left, 132×56, '← Back' (D045). v1.24.2 restored the Timer's portrait_ok flag, lost when a patch script died on an earlier assert and everything queued behind it silently never applied; /health gains panel (the live LVGL resolution) so a silently-borrowed landscape can never again hide from remote verification.

nodes.label: Any orientation; BOOT cycles 90° per press — v1.9.0 / v1.22.0 / v1.24.1
nodes.norm_label: any orientation; boot cycles 90° per press — v1.9.0 / v1.22.0 / v1.24.1
nodes.rationale: v1.9.0: Flip 180 via rotation 2 — the other landscape, identical 600×450, the library re-applies the CST226SE swap and mirror so touch follows; no LVGL re-init, so a live toggle. Fixed during the flash: app_apply_rotation() repaints via lv_scr_act() before beginLvglHelper() ran, so LVGL was uninitialised and the boot call hit NULL — guarded on lv_disp_get_default(). v1.22.0: portrait clock (hours over minutes, no colon — Fliqlo's phone layout); ui_init is re-entrant; apps stay 600×450 and the host lends them the nearest landscape (D043); settings.rotation 0–3 migrates from rotate_180; POST /rotate. v1.24.1: rotation happens IN the app — v1.22.0 sent you to the clock on every BOOT press and being thrown home read as a crash; the live path remembers what was open, rotates, rebuilds the clock and reopens the same app. Stated casualty: rotating inside Settings discards unsaved edits, because create-on-entry apps cannot be rebuilt mid-edit.

nodes.label: Themes — v1.27.0
nodes.rationale: Theme 0 is Fliqlo, untouched. Theme 1 'Pop' is the bento-widget board: blue hour card, red minute card, yellow colon, orange/blue weather pair, palette-cycled drawer tiles, orange chrome, chunkier corners — on the same true black. A Themes app previews each theme from its own color table and applies it as an in-place rebuild (the rotation machinery, minus the rotation). POST /theme and a theme field in /health keep it drivable (D049).

nodes.label: Rotation 0 is natively 600×450 landscape
nodes.rationale: The panel is defined landscape-first in initSequence.h, so no re-layout is needed; landscape rotations carry an internal _offset_y = 16 applied inside pushColors by the driver, while application and LVGL coordinates stay 0-based over 600×450.

nodes.label: The clock could be dragged around: the screen object is on the scroll chain
nodes.norm_label: the clock could be dragged around: the screen object is on the scroll chain
nodes.rationale: Sibling bug found on hardware 2026-08-16. decor() cleared SCROLLABLE but not SCROLL_CHAIN, and lv_scr_act() was never touched at all: the screen is an ordinary lv_obj, scrollable by default and the last stop on the scroll chain, so a drag on the clock was forwarded up the chain and the SCREEN scrolled, taking the whole layout with it. Fix, both halves: clear SCROLL_CHAIN in decor(), and clear SCROLLABLE plus set LV_SCROLLBAR_MODE_OFF on scr_clock in ui_init(). Nothing on the clock screen is ever meant to scroll — the only thing that legitimately moves the layout is the burn-in walk, which sets a position directly.

nodes.label: Apps borrow landscape
nodes.rationale: Native and script apps alike are 600x450 layouts; pretending otherwise clips them at x=450. The host rotates the panel to the nearest landscape (90->0, 270->180) for the duration of an app and restores the owner's orientation on the way out; rotating under a running app is impossible by construction. Superseded for native apps by D045 (App.portrait_ok); still the default for untagged scripts.
nodes.source_file: docs/decisions/D043 - Orientation is the clock's job; apps borrow landscape.md

nodes.label: Three orientation tiers
nodes.rationale: The library supports all four rotations with touch remapping, but every screen was laid out for 600x450 and line-mode zoom renders both cards side by side, 572 px that portrait's 450 cannot hold. So: (1) the clock and drawer are orientation-native (portrait stacks hours over minutes with no colon, as Fliqlo does on a phone; the drawer wraps three tiles wide; ui_init is re-entrant and rebuilds the clock for the new shape, freeing the zoom buffer and killing the old build's timers first); (2) apps borrow landscape; (3) portrait line mode is the fade, not the zoom, since portrait never allocates the canvas. A rotation rebuilds the clock screen and closes any app in progress: orientation is a device-level act.
nodes.source_file: docs/decisions/D043 - Orientation is the clock's job; apps borrow landscape.md

nodes.label: App.portrait_ok contract flag and the script portrait_ok tag
nodes.norm_label: app.portrait_ok contract flag and the script portrait_ok tag
nodes.rationale: True suppresses D043's borrowed landscape; false keeps it, which is now only the scripts' default. A script opts in with a portrait_ok tag in its FIRST line, because the host decides rotation before the script runs so the flag cannot live inside the program, and reads SCREEN_W / SCREEN_H globals to actually branch.

nodes.label: Standard back chip: app_host_std_back()
nodes.rationale: Every app had grown its own back button in its own corner (timer in a control row, Settings mid-bar right, Lab bottom-left, drawer bottom-centre saying 'Clock'). Now one chip: bottom-left, 132x56, charcoal, '<- Back', on every app and the drawer; layouts reserve the bottom-left 156x76; a custom cb only where leaving needs a guard (Settings' unsaved-changes prompt). The drawer's says Back, not Clock: the label names the gesture, not the destination (D033). Uniformity beat v1.14.0's bigger timer buttons where the two collided: Start/Reset became 56-tall strip keys, still 200 px wide.

nodes.label: Applying a theme is a rebuild, not a repaint
nodes.norm_label: applying a theme is a rebuild, not a repaint
nodes.rationale: Every screen is create-on-entry (D026) and the rotation machinery (D043 / v1.24.1) already rebuilds the clock and re-opens the current app in place, so the Themes app saves the choice and calls exactly that; the new look is standing everywhere before the finger lifts. POST /theme {n} does the same through a rebuild request that skips the rotation no-op guard. Known cosmetic: the zoom canvas renders both mini cards in the hour-card colour, so in Pop the live minute card is red while its zoomed ghost is blue for the 350 ms transition.

nodes.label: A theme is a ~12-field colour table (theme.h)
nodes.norm_label: a theme is a ~12-field colour table (theme.h)
nodes.rationale: The owner wanted selectable themes: the Fliqlo look and a second inspired by a board of vivid bento widgets. The table is read at BUILD time by everything that draws cards: the clock (hour and minute cards may differ; Pop makes them blue and red), the colon dots (Pop: yellow), the weather pair (orange/blue), drawer tiles (palette cycled by index), the timer's cards and the standard chip. The background is black in every theme: the panel is an AMOLED, black is free, and the burn-in budget was calibrated to it. Fliqlo stays byte-identical as theme 0; unthemed working screens (Settings, Lab, Messages chrome) are deliberately neutral; a third theme is one table row plus nothing. The Themes app previews with swatches built from the same table, so the preview cannot drift from the truth. The second reference's generative pixel art is a SCREEN, not a palette, and was not attempted.

nodes.label: Native games drawn from the theme table
nodes.norm_label: native games drawn from the theme table
nodes.rationale: Snake and Breakout are not skinned emulations: the snake is the digit colour, the food the chip colour, Breakout's brick rows cycle the tile palette, the ball is the colon yellow in Pop, scores render in fliqlo_mid. Switching themes reskins the arcade for free, D049's cascade doing its job. Sound: none, and games designed FOR silence rather than missing it.

nodes.label: The drawer wraps and scrolls vertically only; tile cells keep SCROLL_CHAIN; row height computed from the live display
nodes.norm_label: the drawer wraps and scrolls vertically only; tile cells keep scroll_chain; row height computed from the live display
nodes.rationale: One flex row silently lost apps past three (678 px in a 600 px row). Vertical-only so it cannot compete with the left-edge back gesture. decor() cleared SCROLL_CHAIN on cells so any drag beginning on a tile died at the cell: right hygiene for ornaments, exactly wrong for a container whose children must pass drags upward. Icon-less script apps show the first letter of their name.

nodes.label: Lab Back moved to a 52 px bottom strip: anywhere in the top 46 px collides with the tab row; Timer and Settings keep Back at the bottom
nodes.norm_label: lab back moved to a 52 px bottom strip: anywhere in the top 46 px collides with the tab row; timer and settings keep back at the bottom
nodes.rationale: Shrinking the tab button matrix would have worked (tabview is a flex column, width set once) but depends on LVGL internals nobody can see; the collision was pointing at an inconsistency, not a coordinate.

nodes.label: app_host_std_back(): one 132x56 "<- Back" chip bottom-left on every app and the drawer; the label names the gesture, not the destination
nodes.norm_label: app_host_std_back(): one 132x56 "<- back" chip bottom-left on every app and the drawer; the label names the gesture, not the destination
nodes.rationale: Settings passes its unsaved-changes guard into the same chip; Timer's tall Start/Reset cards became 56 px strip keys because uniformity beat bigger buttons where they collided. App.portrait_ok records who lays themselves out; scripts tag it on their first line because the host decides rotation before the script runs.

nodes.label: Games are themed, not retro-skinned; two engine templates: the canvas path (Snake, grid redrawn into a PSRAM buffer) and the object path (Breakout, float physics on ms-delta); Jump reuses both plus the visible two-finger zones
nodes.norm_label: games are themed, not retro-skinned; two engine templates: the canvas path (snake, grid redrawn into a psram buffer) and the object path (breakout, float physics on ms-delta); jump reuses both plus the visible two-finger zones
nodes.rationale: Switching themes reskins the arcade - D049's cascade earning its keep where nobody planned it. Fields are computed from the live display so portrait is just a taller game. Gamepad zones draw a dim outline from the same table the hit-test reads so drawing cannot drift from touch.

nodes.label: Orientation in three tiers: clock and drawer orientation-native (portrait stacks the cards), apps borrow the nearest landscape, portrait line mode takes the no-canvas fade; ui_init re-entrant
nodes.norm_label: orientation in three tiers: clock and drawer orientation-native (portrait stacks the cards), apps borrow the nearest landscape, portrait line mode takes the no-canvas fade; ui_init re-entrant
nodes.rationale: The line mode zoom canvas renders 572 px that portrait cannot hold. The ui_init prologue kills the previous build's timers, frees the 265 KB zoom buffer and NULLs every lazily-created static because objects die with the old screen but statics do not. The first remote cycle test caught a phantom BOOT press: the "external 10K pull-up" in our own reference note was unverified; INPUT_PULLUP fixed it.

nodes.rationale: Selects the T4-S3 explicitly instead of begin() auto-detect; ends with setRotation(0); calls SY.enableMeasure() and SY.disableOTG().

nodes.rationale: lv_init, one full-screen ps_malloc buffer (600x450x2 = 540000 B in PSRAM), disp_flush -> pushColors, touch indev when hasTouch(), and a rounder_cb snapping flush areas to even coordinates.

nodes.label: beginLvglHelperDMA()
nodes.rationale: Two 1/10-screen MALLOC_CAP_DMA buffers (~54 KB each of internal SRAM): faster flush but spends scarce internal RAM; rejected in D009.

nodes.norm_label: cst226se capacitive touch (i2c, sda 6 / scl 7, irq 8, rst 17)
nodes.rationale: Probed with Wire.beginTransmission() before init; if it does not ACK the library continues with touch offline rather than failing begin(). Limits and axis swap/mirror re-applied on every setRotation().

nodes.label: The red charge LED stops blinking — v1.7.6

nodes.label: The SY6970 status LED reports a fault, not power (reversal)
nodes.norm_label: the sy6970 status led reports a fault, not power (reversal)
nodes.rationale: The original reasoning was that the status LED is a useful 'it has power' signal, trivially reversible if distracting next to a pure-black AMOLED. It was: there is no battery, so the charger can never complete a cycle, and a blinking red LED is exactly how the SY6970 says so — correct behaviour describing a condition that will never change and nobody needs to know about. On a desk object whose point is a black panel with pixels genuinely off, a red light flashing forever is the only thing in the room that looks broken. SY.disableStatLed() silences it; charging is unaffected because there is nothing to charge.

nodes.label: Activity states
nodes.rationale: The device's primary job is to show what is being worked on right now; emotions are secondary. Activities: reading, editing, building, testing, flashing, debugging, searching, thinking, waiting. Emotions (success, error, celebrate, frustrated, confused, relief, proud, sleepy…) only when they say something an activity cannot. The line vibrates in proportion to the process — amplitude, frequency and speed scale with the state's arousal: waiting ~11 px, reading gentle, building ~40 px, flashing ~61 px — so the state that matches the real intensity reads correctly from across the room.

nodes.label: Emotion API
nodes.rationale: The clock can express what we are doing. Two transports — HTTP POST /emotion and BLE Nordic UART — carry identical JSON {state, duration_s, message}. duration_s defaults to 5 and is clamped to 300; bad input returns 400 with a reason and never reboots the device. The full set is 32 states; GET /health and emotion_from_name() are the authority. clear/none/stop/idle revert immediately: the line fades, the clock slides back to centre, the weather returns — the clock is the default state of this object and an animation is a temporary visitor.

nodes.label: flipclock global command
nodes.rationale: flipclock is installed at ~/.local/bin/flipclock and instructed from ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, so the display works from any conversation in any directory; tools/say and tools/hush are thin wrappers kept for muscle memory. tools/flipclock.py is the Python client that speaks HTTP or BLE (auto: HTTP first, BLE fallback) and is importable (emote()).

nodes.label: Hard constraints
nodes.rationale: LVGL 8.4.0 pinned — LV_Helper.cpp is #if LVGL_VERSION_MAJOR == 8, so upgrading breaks the link, not just the API. Board settings copied verbatim from the library — every flag is load-bearing. No TFT_eSPI — it has no QSPI transport. No BLE in v1 (the later HID phase). No deep sleep, no battery logic — USB-powered, always on. config.h holds first-boot defaults only: read settings_get(), never a DEFAULT_* macro, outside settings_reset(). Wi-Fi credentials are never in a file — typed on the device. Position self-aligning widgets with lv_obj_align(), never lv_obj_set_pos(): in LVGL 8 alignment is a persistent style property, so set_pos on an aligned object is an offset from the alignment point. Any decorative lv_obj_create() must call decor(). Never call LVGL from a non-LVGL task.

nodes.label: tools/hush as the last action of every turn
nodes.norm_label: tools/hush as the last action of every turn
nodes.rationale: The panel shows what is being done, so when work stops the display should stop; anything left on screen after the turn is dead time. This reverses an earlier never-hush rule, which existed because state was pushed only once at the start of a turn and hushing killed the only signal — prefixing every command removed that problem and made hushing correct again.

nodes.label: Keep it lit while you work
nodes.norm_label: keep it lit while you work
nodes.rationale: The owner built this device to see what Claude is doing from across the desk; a dark screen during a long stretch of work defeats the point of the object, and they have called this out more than once. Push a state at the start of every turn and refresh at each major step; pushes only happen at tool-call boundaries, so cover pure-reasoning gaps with a duration that spans the expected work; if the device does not answer, carry on silently and never block work on it.

nodes.label: message is an object, never a verb
nodes.norm_label: message is an object, never a verb
nodes.rationale: The caption renders state + message, so the state already supplies the verb: building + "ui.cpp" shows 'building  ui.cpp'; message "reading" would render 'reading reading'. ≤ 48 chars, wraps to two lines; no jokes, no status restatements. Convention recorded here at v1.6.0.

nodes.label: Prefix the work command with tools/say
nodes.norm_label: prefix the work command with tools/say
nodes.rationale: Pushing the state as its own separate call is a step that gets skipped once a turn runs long — it failed twice in practice, both times noticed by the owner. Attaching it to the work command (tools/say building "ui.cpp" && pio run) makes it part of the thing being done. say is fire-and-forget, capped at 2 s, always exits 0, so it cannot delay or break the command it prefixes. Conversational turns count too: run tools/say thinking before answering anything substantive.

nodes.label: Semantic versioning and release procedure
nodes.rationale: include/version.h is the single source of truth. MAJOR for a breaking HTTP/BLE API or settings-schema change, MINOR for a new capability (transport, screen, feature), PATCH for fixes. Every release: bump FW_VERSION_*, append docs/RELEASES.md, commit and tag, flash and confirm via GET /health — on the DEVICE, not in the tree. Trust FW_GIT over FW_BUILD: FW_BUILD is __DATE__/__TIME__ baked in when main.cpp compiles and goes stale when any other file changes; FW_GIT is injected as a build flag by scripts/version_stamp.py so a change forces a rebuild; +dirty marks uncommitted changes in the image.

nodes.label: Serial port detection by USB ID 303A:1001
nodes.norm_label: serial port detection by usb id 303a:1001
nodes.rationale: The serial port is named after the physical USB socket, so moving the cable renames it — usbmodem2101 became usbmodem1101 mid-session and the upload failed with a bare Error 2. 0x303A:0x1001 is the ESP32-S3 USB-JTAG identity and never changes, so the port is detected from `pio device list --json-output` by hwid instead of being hardcoded.

nodes.label: Short durations, refreshed
nodes.rationale: The 30 s default is deliberate: every prefixed command refreshes the timer, so the duration only has to outlive the gap between commands, not the whole task. What the owner sees idle is the tail after the LAST push, so a long duration parks the line on screen after the work finished; if the session crashes, the device returns to the clock within half a minute. Pass a bigger number only for one genuinely long command.

nodes.label: Working agreements
nodes.rationale: Read the decisions before changing anything structural — disagree by writing a superseding decision note, never by silently contradicting one. Update log.md (append-only, newest at the bottom) after any session that changes the project. Stages are hardware-gated: the owner flashes and verifies each on real hardware before the next begins. Ground truth is the library source at ~/.local/src/LilyGo-AMOLED-Series, not the README.

nodes.label: RM690B0 panel over QSPI
nodes.rationale: The panel is configured with four data lines d0..d3, cmdBit = 8, addBit = 24 and pushed through spi_device_handle_t; a library without a QSPI transport cannot address it. bodmer/TFT_eSPI @ 2.5.31 still appears in lib_deps only because other examples in the library repo reference it — kept rather than pruned, per D003.

nodes.label: The two halves of the transition are strictly sequential — v1.4.0
nodes.norm_label: the two halves of the transition are strictly sequential — v1.4.0
nodes.rationale: In: scale the clock into the corner, THEN the line appears. Out: the line disappears, THEN the clock scales back. Overlapping read as two unrelated things happening at once; in sequence it reads as one movement — the clock gets out of the way and the line takes the space it vacated. A one-shot timer at the end of the flight creates the line; leaving, the fade-out drives the hand-off. A state change while the line is up does not re-run the transition — activities change every few seconds and re-flying the clock each time would be unwatchable; only the caption swaps.

nodes.rationale: The same rule the weather task follows; the third time it mattered in the project, so it became the house rule in CLAUDE.md. Failure mode is a crash that is hard to find.

nodes.label: Rule 1: create on entry, destroy on exit
nodes.norm_label: rule 1: create on entry, destroy on exit
nodes.rationale: No app keeps a screen alive in the background. Settings has done this all along, which is why PSRAM stays at ~7.3 MB free with a 527 KB framebuffer and a 265 KB zoom canvas resident.
nodes.source_file: docs/decisions/D026 - Apps are a platform, not a special case.md

nodes.label: Rule 3: decor() every decorative object
nodes.rationale: LVGL sets CLICKABLE and SCROLL_CHAIN on everything; leaving them on breaks the host's gestures from inside the app (D014).
nodes.source_file: docs/decisions/D026 - Apps are a platform, not a special case.md

nodes.label: Rule 2: never touch the clock's objects; the host mediates
nodes.norm_label: rule 2: never touch the clock's objects; the host mediates
nodes.rationale: Same discipline as the threading rule - the failure mode is identical and just as hard to find.
nodes.source_file: docs/decisions/D026 - Apps are a platform, not a special case.md

nodes.label: Rule 4: only draw from the LVGL task
nodes.norm_label: rule 4: only draw from the lvgl task
nodes.rationale: Cross-reference to D018's queue rule; app code runs on the LVGL task and must not be driven from other tasks.
nodes.source_file: docs/decisions/D026 - Apps are a platform, not a special case.md

nodes.label: The internal I2C bus (6/7) is scannable, never drivable
nodes.norm_label: the internal i2c bus (6/7) is scannable, never drivable
nodes.rationale: An address probe is a read, so the scanner may run on the live PMU/touch bus (it shows the P4 plug too). The external scanner uses the second controller Wire1 on whitelist pins only - reconfiguring Wire would yank the bus out from under the touch driver. I2C scan runs synchronously on the LVGL task (~150 ms freeze), accepted as cosmetic.

nodes.label: Leave no trace: destroy() returns every whitelist pin to Hi-Z
nodes.norm_label: leave no trace: destroy() returns every whitelist pin to hi-z
nodes.rationale: Closes Serial1, ends Wire1. Launching and leaving the Lab is electrically invisible. Known sharp edge: the three tabs share the whitelist and trust the user - last-configured wins; a bench tool for its owner, not a product.
nodes.source_file: docs/decisions/D035 - The Lab may only touch pins the firmware does not own.md

nodes.label: A fresh lua_State per launch
nodes.rationale: Created in create(), closed in destroy(), so 'create on entry, destroy on exit' holds for scripts exactly as for native apps and nothing leaks from one run into the next.

nodes.label: A hybrid: the core stays C++, the app layer gains a Lua 5.4 runtime
nodes.norm_label: a hybrid: the core stays c++, the app layer gains a lua 5.4 runtime
nodes.rationale: Scripts are slower than C++; anything doing per-frame maths should still be a native app - the runtime is for the long tail. Adding an app is tools/app add foo.lua: under a second, no reboot, the clock never stops (verified live 2026-08-22 including delete and re-add).

nodes.label: A 400 k VM-instruction budget per entry point is the whole safety story
nodes.norm_label: a 400 k vm-instruction budget per entry point is the whole safety story
nodes.rationale: Scripts run on the LVGL task - that is why they may touch LVGL safely - which also means 'while true do end' would freeze the clock with the cable as the only way out. A LUA_MASKCOUNT hook stops any entry point past 400 k instructions and reports it on screen: generous for building a screen, absurd for a tick. No preemption: a binding that blocks still blocks.

nodes.label: Lua allocates from PSRAM, never the internal heap
nodes.norm_label: lua allocates from psram, never the internal heap
nodes.rationale: 8 MB of PSRAM against ~60 KB of internal heap in use; a leaking script must not be able to starve the display driver, which allocates internally.

nodes.label: text/plain uploads arrive empty
nodes.rationale: ESPAsyncWebServer special-cases Content-Type: text/plain: if the body starts with param-like characters and contains '=', it parses the whole thing as form data and never calls the body handler. Lua source is full of '='. tools/app sends application/octet-stream, as OTA already did. Symptom: an empty upload with no error anywhere.

nodes.label: Compile at upload, not at launch
nodes.norm_label: compile at upload, not at launch
nodes.rationale: A syntax error is rejected at upload with the parser's own message and any previous working version of that name is never touched.

nodes.label: Instruction budget (LUA_MASKCOUNT hook, ~400k instructions per entry point)
nodes.norm_label: instruction budget (lua_maskcount hook, ~400k instructions per entry point)
nodes.rationale: Scripts run on the LVGL task (which is why they may touch LVGL safely), so while true do end would freeze the clock with the cable as the only way out; the budget stops it and says so on screen.

nodes.label: Lua PSRAM allocator and fresh lua_State per launch
nodes.norm_label: lua psram allocator and fresh lua_state per launch
nodes.rationale: A leaking script must not be able to starve the display driver of the ~60 KB internal heap; a fresh state per launch makes scripts obey create-on-entry / destroy-on-exit exactly as native apps do.

nodes.label: Lua 5.4.7 vendored verbatim (MIT) minus lua.c / luac.c
nodes.norm_label: lua 5.4.7 vendored verbatim (mit) minus lua.c / luac.c
nodes.rationale: Registry entries are third-party wrappers of varying maintenance; Lua's own source is ~15k lines of dependency-free C89 that has compiled everywhere for twenty years. Vendoring makes the version a fact of this repo rather than a resolution result. lua.c and luac.c both define main().

nodes.label: luaconf.h as shipped - do not edit; project changes are -D flags in library.json
nodes.norm_label: luaconf.h as shipped - do not edit; project changes are -d flags in library.json
nodes.rationale: So the next version bump stays a directory copy.

nodes.label: Any Lua API error outside lua_pcall calls abort(); lua_atpanic now longjmps back into script_create, shows the message and closes the state
nodes.norm_label: any lua api error outside lua_pcall calls abort(); lua_atpanic now longjmps back into script_create, shows the message and closes the state
nodes.rationale: The version error was raised inside luaL_requiref, called directly. Errors inside script code were always protected; the runtime's own setup was not, breaking D037's promise that a broken script fails alone.

nodes.label: Four Lua safety choices: fresh lua_State per launch, PSRAM allocator, instruction budget, compile at upload; io/os/package/debug not loaded
nodes.norm_label: four lua safety choices: fresh lua_state per launch, psram allocator, instruction budget, compile at upload; io/os/package/debug not loaded
nodes.rationale: Each chosen for a named failure: leaked state, a leaking script starving the display driver, a runaway loop freezing the LVGL task, a broken upload clobbering a working app. +148 KB flash, +1 KB RAM, measured.

nodes.norm_label: -dlua_use_c89=0 turned c89 mode on: luaconf.h tests lua_32bits by value but lua_use_c89 by defined(); library.json flags do not reach consumers
nodes.rationale: lua_Integer was long (4 bytes) inside lib/lua and long long (8) in script.cpp, so luaL_checkversion reported different numeric types.

nodes.norm_label: silent, and said so: no dac, amp or speaker
nodes.rationale: The board has no audio path (T4-S3 note), so the player is a moving picture. The day a MAX98357A lands on the Lab pins, audio becomes an I2S task; until then, no pretending.

nodes.label: Canvas path (Snake) and object path (Breakout) as engine templates
nodes.norm_label: canvas path (snake) and object path (breakout) as engine templates
nodes.rationale: Snake proves the canvas path: grid redrawn per step into a PSRAM buffer allocated on enter and freed on leave. Breakout proves the object path: float physics with ms-delta, 'english' off the paddle edge, axis-picked brick bounce. Between them most 8-bit genres have a template. esp_random() seeds gameplay; no Date/rand() ceremony.

nodes.label: One Games app: a chooser, then the game, with the in-app back stack
nodes.norm_label: one games app: a chooser, then the game, with the in-app back stack
nodes.rationale: The owner asked for 8-bit games, both recreated classics and a real Game Boy. One app holds all of it using the in-app back stack the platform already taught every other app. Game Boy shipped as the third card, honestly greyed: it needed Peanut-GB's source and a homebrew ROM, downloads the owner approves rather than bundled silently; the card said so. Ninth native app; the drawer scrolls, as designed.

nodes.label: Touch grammar per game, no buttons on the field
nodes.norm_label: touch grammar per game, no buttons on the field
nodes.rationale: Snake steers by swipe (reversal into yourself is ignored); Breakout's paddle rides the finger and a tap serves. Death -> score + best (NVS) + tap to retry. Both lay out from the live display: the snake grid and brick wall are computed, not constant, so portrait simply gets a taller field (D045).

nodes.norm_label: cartridges are files: post /rom, the /roms shelf, per-cart battery saves
nodes.rationale: POST /rom uploads a cartridge (tools/rom keeps filenames); every /roms/*.gb is a cartridge, a picker appears when there is more than one, and battery saves persist per cart to a .sav on exit for carts that have RAM (v1.36.0 turned the single boot.gb slot into a shelf). nodes.norm_label: screen doubled to 320x288 on a canvas in dmg green, pre-swapped for lv_color_16_swap

nodes.label: Peanut-GB vendored verbatim into lib/peanut-gb/
nodes.rationale: The owner downloaded Peanut-GB (MIT, Mahyar Koshkouei) themselves and said 'go get the gameboy'. Sound is compiled out (ENABLE_SOUND 0): the silence is hardware, not configuration. Frame pacing is one gb_run_frame() per 16 ms on the LVGL task (a few ms at 240 MHz) with a full-canvas invalidate per frame; the knobs if it ever tears are invalidate-every-second-frame and PEANUT_GB_HIGH_LCD_ACCURACY. DMG-only: Game Boy Color-exclusive carts refuse politely. ~330 KB PSRAM while playing (ROM + canvas + core), all freed on exit.

nodes.label: The gamepad is raw touch zones read two points at once (app_touch_points())
nodes.norm_label: the gamepad is raw touch zones read two points at once (app_touch_points())
nodes.rationale: D-pad plus button simultaneously is two fingers, which LVGL's single-point indev can never report, so app_touch_points() extends the trackpad's raw-read precedent (D051). Landscape: screen left, pad column right; portrait: screen top, thumbs below, like a phone emulator. The zones shipped invisible (hitboxes with no chrome, reported by the owner within the hour); they now draw themselves from the same table the hit-test reads (v1.35.1).

nodes.label: A real Game Boy: Peanut-GB vendored verbatim (MIT), DMG greens at 2x, sound compiled out, Libbet (zlib) as the shipped cart; /roms/*.gb shelf with per-cart saves; boot.gb removed
nodes.norm_label: a real game boy: peanut-gb vendored verbatim (mit), dmg greens at 2x, sound compiled out, libbet (zlib) as the shipped cart; /roms/*.gb shelf with per-cart saves; boot.gb removed
nodes.rationale: The core was a download the owner approved, not bundled silently. Tobu Tobu Girl ships no prebuilt ROM. The picker once wiped its own choice because game_close() unconditionally cleared gb_cart_path; the wipe is now conditional on the owner leaving.

nodes.label: Two-finger input reads the CST226's raw point count / points (app_touch_count, app_touch_points) while a press is live
nodes.norm_label: two-finger input reads the cst226's raw point count / points (app_touch_count, app_touch_points) while a press is live
nodes.rationale: LVGL's pointer indev reports exactly one finger, forever; this is the one place the firmware reads the touch controller outside the LVGL helper, with the double-read risk stated. A click is DOWN then UP ~30 ms apart and destroy() fires an unconditional all-up so a phantom held button cannot survive the app.

nodes.label: Save and Close are separate, with a guard — v1.2.0
nodes.norm_label: save and close are separate, with a guard — v1.2.0
nodes.rationale: One 'Save & close' gave no way to back out, and it mattered because the brightness sliders preview live: a user who dragged one and left had already changed the device with nothing to undo it. Save commits and stays open ('Saved' for ~2 s); Close with unsaved edits asks Discard / Keep editing; Discard restores the snapshot taken when the screen opened and undoes the live effects, NVS untouched. Save lights up blue whenever there is something unsaved. Sliders no longer write into settings_get() — they preview only, and the committed value is read from the widget on Save; without that, Discard would have had nothing to restore. Explicit apply-now actions (Connect, city pick, Apply & sync NTP, Reset) take a fresh snapshot.

nodes.label: A Save button must save everything on the screen
nodes.norm_label: a save button must save everything on the screen
nodes.rationale: Follow-up: originally credentials were committed only by the Connect button, so picking a network, typing the password and tapping Save & close — the obvious thing, and what every other setting on the screen responds to — silently discarded both. close_cb() now commits the picked SSID and any typed password alongside everything else and calls net_apply_wifi() when either changed. Any field a Save button does not persist is a trap, no matter how reasonable the split looked while writing it; Connect remains the apply-it-right-now shortcut, no longer the only path.

nodes.label: Settings on its own LVGL screen (lv_obj_create(NULL)), deleted on close
nodes.norm_label: settings on its own lvgl screen (lv_obj_create(null)), deleted on close
nodes.rationale: The clock screen is never disturbed and returns exactly as it was; the clock loop skips all its work while Settings is open so no flip fires behind the menu and the burn-in walk does not move an invisible screen.

nodes.label: Lua 5.4.7 vendored verbatim into lib/lua/
nodes.rationale: Minus lua.c/luac.c. Not from the PlatformIO registry - those are third-party wrappers of varying maintenance, while Lua's own source is dependency-free C that has compiled everywhere for twenty years. Vendoring makes the version a fact of the repo, not a resolution result. Measured cost: +148 KB flash (27.3% -> 30.0%), +1 KB RAM.

nodes.label: App drawer
nodes.rationale: Swipe up from the bottom edge: Timer, Settings, the Lab (GPIO/I2C/UART), Messages (D046), Themes (D049), YouTube (D050/D053/D054), Games — Snake, Breakout, Jump, Game Boy (D055/D056), Browser via headless Chrome on the Mac (D057), Equalizer (D058), Trackpad and Keyboard as real BLE HID (D051/D052), plus any Lua apps. The drawer wraps and scrolls; the full remote surface is docs/reference/HTTP API.md.

nodes.label: Companion pattern: the Mac does what the device cannot; the device shows honest pixels
nodes.norm_label: companion pattern: the mac does what the device cannot; the device shows honest pixels
nodes.rationale: The Mac carries the walls the board cannot (codec, stream acquisition, JavaScript, system audio); the clock receives a wire format it can decode with what it has and shows real pixels or real levels. The breakable links (yt-dlp, cookie extraction, Chrome) live Mac-side where fixing them is 'brew upgrade', never in firmware. Instances: YouTube playback (D053), Home (D054), the browser (D057), the equalizer (D058), with tools/ytserve as the single companion process.

nodes.label: Privacy line: the owner's session stays on the Mac; the device gets ids, titles, pixels or bar heights
nodes.norm_label: privacy line: the owner's session stays on the mac; the device gets ids, titles, pixels or bar heights
nodes.rationale: Cookies are read by yt-dlp, on the owner's Mac, from the owner's browser, and never leave that machine; the device receives video ids and titles and nothing is stored anywhere new. D057 draws the same line for the browser (Chrome browses with the Mac's sessions; only pixels come down, only coordinates and keystrokes go up) and D058 the tightest yet (thirty-two loudness numbers thirty times a second, nothing reconstructable).

nodes.label: On-device playback walled off three ways
nodes.norm_label: on-device playback walled off three ways
nodes.rationale: No hardware codec (software H.264 is single-digit fps on this CPU), stream acquisition is the signed-URL cat-and-mouse that breaks monthly, and the board has no audio path at all. The owner chose Tier A: official Data API, thumbnails, tap-to-play throwing the video to the Mac. D053 later carries two of the walls on the Mac; the third is physics.

nodes.label: The Mac transcodes to MJPEG; the clock decodes the latest complete frame
nodes.norm_label: the mac transcodes to mjpeg; the clock decodes the latest complete frame
nodes.rationale: tools/ytserve gains /stream/<id>: yt-dlp resolves the direct URL, ffmpeg emits baseline MJPEG at 320x180, 12 fps, ~q9, a bitrate the Wi-Fi budget yawns at. The clock's worker reads the stream into a rolling buffer, frames on SOI/EOI, decodes the LATEST complete frame and drops stale ones, a natural frame-skip when decode (~35 ms) lags; the LVGL task only ever blits the front of a double buffer. ~230 KB PSRAM for two 320x180 buffers, allocated once on first play and reused. Playback occupies the yt worker; leaving the app or the player always stops the stream. yt-dlp is a Mac-side install the owner makes; until then the player reports 'companion: install yt-dlp'.

nodes.label: Companion /home via yt-dlp --cookies-from-browser
nodes.rationale: The official API cannot provide Home at any auth level (D050 addendum), but yt-dlp can read the owner's own logged-in browser session and fetch youtube.com/feed/recommended, the actual personalized Home. The companion tries Chrome, then Firefox, then Safari and returns the top ~12 as {id, title, channel}; the clock builds thumbnails from public i.ytimg.com URLs. Home is the app's default view whenever a companion host is configured, which is what 'like my phone' means; Latest / Popular / Search remain as chips. Requires yt-dlp, a logged-in browser, and possibly a one-time keychain approval; each failure reports as its own message. Cookie extraction is the most breakable link in the stack and lives Mac-side.

nodes.label: Video-only format selector for /stream
nodes.rationale: Playback failed on most real videos because the /stream selector demanded MUXED streams and modern YouTube ships many videos adaptive-only. Video-only formats are the right ask: the clock has no audio and ffmpeg drops it anyway. bestvideo[height<=360]/.../best, verified against the exact id that failed.
nodes.source_file: docs/decisions/D054 - Home comes from the owner's own session.md

nodes.label: The Mac renders in headless Chrome; the clock is a thin client
nodes.norm_label: the mac renders in headless chrome; the clock is a thin client
nodes.rationale: A from-scratch browser for the modern web is impossible on this board (sites assume a JIT, gigabytes of RAM and a GPU; the board has 8 MB PSRAM and none of the rest) and saying otherwise would be a lie. But Opera Mini, Puffin and Amazon Silk were real browsers that rendered on a server and sent the client a picture, exactly the pattern the YouTube player proved (D053). The companion drives Playwright with channel='chrome' (the SYSTEM Chrome 151, no Chromium download) and streams JPEG frames, the wire format the YouTube player already decodes; the clock decodes the latest frame into a full-screen RGB565 double buffer (browser.cpp reuses yt.cpp's TJpgDec path in spirit, pre-swapped for LV_COLOR_16_SWAP). Honest costs: only works while the companion runs; a remote-control feel at ~5 fps, not a snappy local browser; fidelity is Chrome's, complete. ~1 MB PSRAM while open, freed on exit; the worker joins before the buffers are released so nothing decodes into freed memory. The companion host is shared: browser_begin() seeds the IP from yt_play_host().

nodes.label: Native reader and companion reader-mode: rejected as the primary
nodes.norm_label: native reader and companion reader-mode: rejected as the primary
nodes.rationale: A native on-device HTML reader with no companion is real work for a result that fails on essentially every mainstream site (a possible future add for offline reading). A companion reader-mode that de-clutters to article text is fast and crisp but article-shaped only, with no logins and no interaction (a cheap future add on the same companion).
nodes.source_file: docs/decisions/D057 - The clock is a browser, through the Mac.md

nodes.label: The Mac captures its own output; the clock draws the bars
nodes.norm_label: the mac captures its own output; the clock draws the bars
nodes.rationale: The clock has no microphone and a microphone would be the wrong instrument anyway: it hears the room, not the mix. The signal that matters is the Mac's own output and only the Mac can hear it. The companion pattern for the fourth time (D053, D054, D057), with the lightest payload yet. Privacy line, the tightest yet: audio never leaves the Mac; the clock receives thirty-two loudness numbers thirty times a second, not audio, not words, nothing reconstructable. Eleventh native app.

nodes.norm_label: real home (v1.33.0): ytserve /home runs yt-dlp --cookies-from-browser against the owner's own browser session; cookies never leave the mac, the clock sees ids and titles

nodes.label: On-clock player (v1.32.0): ytserve /stream/<id> = yt-dlp -g | ffmpeg -> baseline MJPEG 320x180 @12 fps; the yt worker frames on SOI/EOI, decodes only the latest complete frame, double-buffers in PSRAM; the LVGL task blits

nodes.rationale: The Mac carries the two walls that were policy (codec, stream extraction - yt-dlp lives where brew can update it) and the clock carries the one that is physics (no audio). Frame-skip comes free when the ~35 ms decode lags. Video-only formats are the correct request for a silent device (muxed formats failed for real ids). Back/leave always stops the stream.

nodes.label: The clock is a browser (v1.38.0): headless system Chrome via Playwright renders on the Mac, ~9 ms/frame; concatenated JPEGs down, tap/scroll/key up; browser.cpp is two worker tasks that never touch LVGL
nodes.norm_label: the clock is a browser (v1.38.0): headless system chrome via playwright renders on the mac, ~9 ms/frame; concatenated jpegs down, tap/scroll/key up; browser.cpp is two worker tasks that never touch lvgl
nodes.rationale: A real browser for the modern web cannot run on this board (megabytes of JS, no JIT, no GPU, 8 MB PSRAM); the Opera Mini / Puffin thin-client architecture is the pattern the YouTube player already proved. Chrome browses with the Mac's own sessions; the device sends coordinates and keystrokes and receives JPEGs, never a cookie. Verified with a Wikipedia "Flip clock" article on the flip clock.

nodes.label: The clock is a Bluetooth trackpad and keyboard — v1.29.0 / v1.30.0
nodes.norm_label: the clock is a bluetooth trackpad and keyboard — v1.29.0 / v1.30.0
nodes.rationale: A standard mouse (Report ID 2) joined both HID identities, so the paired Mac sees a real pointing device — no companion: one finger moves (1.5 gain, fractional carry), a still tap left-clicks, a two-finger tap right-clicks (raw CST226 point count; LVGL only ever sees finger one), two-finger drag scrolls; leaving the app releases every button (D051). v1.30.0: a keyboard collection (Report ID 3); the stock LVGL keyboard drives the HOST via an ASCII→usage table, press+release in one call so nothing can stick; D022 revised, not repealed — the gadget IS an input device now, on request (D052). Re-pair required each time: hosts cache the HID descriptor per bond.

nodes.label: Scope boundaries for v1
nodes.rationale: BLE HID input arrived in v1.29-v1.30 (D021's discoverability-only stance is history, kept for the reasoning); battery telemetry exists since v1.21.0 but reacting to it does not; SD slot unused, pins lendable to the Lab; no cloud beyond Open-Meteo and NTP; all rendering local.

nodes.label: 31-byte advertising payload: name (and HID UUID 0x1812 + appearance) in the primary packet, 128-bit NUS UUID in the scan response
nodes.norm_label: 31-byte advertising payload: name (and hid uuid 0x1812 + appearance) in the primary packet, 128-bit nus uuid in the scan response
nodes.rationale: The 18-byte NUS UUID had silently demoted the name to the scan response so passive scanners saw "(unnamed)".

nodes.label: D021 - BLE HID, for discoverability not typing
nodes.norm_label: d021 - ble hid, for discoverability not typing
nodes.rationale: Owner wanted to see and connect to the device from macOS Bluetooth settings. That list only shows profiles macOS can pair with (HID, audio, classic BT); a custom GATT peripheral is invisible by design. So the device advertises a BLE HID keyboard service beside NUS. Supersedes the brief's deferral of the HID phase; the keyboard descriptor was itself superseded by D022.

nodes.norm_label: d022 - custom hid identity, not a keyboard

nodes.label: 31-byte advertising budget
nodes.rationale: Primary packet: flags 3 + appearance 4 + 16-bit HID service 4 + name 'Flip Clock' 12 = 23 bytes. The 128-bit NUS UUID is 18 bytes and cannot share it, so it lives in the scan response.

nodes.label: A keyboard that never types: HID purely for listing
nodes.norm_label: a keyboard that never types: hid purely for listing
nodes.rationale: No key reports are ever sent; the HID service exists as the ticket into System Settings > Bluetooth. Both the appearance 0x03C1 and the 16-bit service UUID 0x1812 are required; macOS uses them together to classify a pairable input device. Emotion API still travels over NUS.

nodes.label: Mandatory pairing, Just Works, no passkey
nodes.norm_label: mandatory pairing, just works, no passkey
nodes.rationale: HID characteristics must be encrypted so pairing is mandatory (bond=true, mitm=false, sc=true; NO_INPUT_OUTPUT). MITM would need a 6-digit code mid-pairing, hijacking the clock face, and protects nothing on a device that sends no keystrokes. Wart: macOS may open Keyboard Setup Assistant on first pair.
nodes.source_file: docs/decisions/D021 - BLE HID, for discoverability not typing.md

nodes.label: Hosts cache the HID descriptor per bond
nodes.norm_label: hosts cache the hid descriptor per bond
nodes.rationale: The descriptor is read once at pairing and cached against the bond, so flipping the identity switch on a paired device changes nothing. To switch: Forget This Device on macOS, Clear pairings on the device, pair again. Skipping this is the most likely reason the change appears to do nothing.

nodes.label: The HID report descriptor, not the appearance, decides what the OS thinks the device is
nodes.norm_label: the hid report descriptor, not the appearance, decides what the os thinks the device is
nodes.rationale: Three layers changed together: report descriptor Generic Desktop/Keyboard -> vendor page 0xFF00 usage 0x01; GAP appearance 0x03C1 Keyboard -> 0x03C0 Generic HID; DIS model string 'Flip Clock Desktop Gadget'. Appearance only picks an icon; a vendor-defined usage page has no OS-level meaning so macOS cannot mistake it for a text-input device, and Keyboard Setup Assistant disappears.
nodes.source_file: docs/decisions/D022 - Custom HID identity, not a keyboard.md

nodes.label: Relative-mouse HID collection (Report ID 2) in both report maps
nodes.norm_label: relative-mouse hid collection (report id 2) in both report maps
nodes.rationale: The v1 scope always said HID input was a later phase; this is that phase arriving for the pointer. A pointing device does not summon Keyboard Setup Assistant, so the gadget identity (D022) keeps its meaning while gaining a cursor; the keyboard fallback identity gains the same collection. ble_mouse(buttons, dx, dy, wheel) is the whole API: no companion, no protocol, system-wide cursor on whatever host is paired. Hosts cache the report map per bond, so re-pairing is mandatory: until the Mac forgets the device and the clock clears its pairings, mouse reports fall on a host that believes the old descriptor and nothing moves or errors.

nodes.label: Keyboard HID collection (Report ID 3) in both report maps
nodes.norm_label: keyboard hid collection (report id 3) in both report maps
nodes.rationale: Typing needs a HID keyboard usage, the exact thing D022 was built to avoid presenting when the fear was macOS mistaking the gadget for a keyboard it was not. D022 is revised, not repealed: the vendor identity still leads and the device still calls itself a desktop gadget, but it genuinely IS a text-input device when the Keyboard app is open, and an identity that follows function is not a mistake. Keyboard Setup Assistant may appear once after re-pairing; close it, usage codes are layout-independent. Third identity revision, one more re-pair; after this the HID surface is complete: vendor + mouse + keyboard.
