nodes.label: BLE HID service purely as the ticket into macOS Bluetooth settings; a keyboard that never types; Just Works pairing
nodes.norm_label: ble hid service purely as the ticket into macos bluetooth settings; a keyboard that never types; just works pairing
nodes.rationale: macOS lists only devices implementing a profile it can pair with; MITM protection would hijack the clock face with a passkey to protect a device that transmits nothing. Pairable switch and Clear pairings as escape hatches.

nodes.label: Custom HID identity: vendor page 0xFF00, appearance 0x03C0, DIS model string; output report wired to the emotion engine
nodes.norm_label: custom hid identity: vendor page 0xff00, appearance 0x03c0, dis model string; output report wired to the emotion engine
nodes.rationale: The report descriptor, not the appearance, is what the OS parses to decide what the device is; a vendor-defined usage page cannot be mistaken for text input. Keyboard descriptor kept behind a fallback switch because a purely vendor-defined descriptor is less certain across OS versions.

nodes.label: Hosts cache the HID descriptor per bond: forget on the Mac, Clear pairings on the clock, pair again after any map change
nodes.norm_label: hosts cache the hid descriptor per bond: forget on the mac, clear pairings on the clock, pair again after any map change

nodes.label: Mouse collection (Report ID 2) and keyboard collection (ID 3) added to the gadget map; the fallback identity types on its native ID1 report
nodes.norm_label: mouse collection (report id 2) and keyboard collection (id 3) added to the gadget map; the fallback identity types on its native id1 report
nodes.rationale: A pointing device does not wake Keyboard Setup Assistant so the gadget identity survives; D022 is revised not repealed - being an input device on purpose is identity following function. ble_key sends press and release in one call because a stuck key must not depend on a second call.

nodes.label: A map carrying two keyboard collections is rejected whole by some hosts, silently; /health ble.subs{mouse,key} via getSubscribedCount()
nodes.norm_label: a map carrying two keyboard collections is rejected whole by some hosts, silently; /health ble.subs{mouse,key} via getsubscribedcount()
nodes.rationale: A bonded host that paired against an older map subscribes to nothing new; every HID surface change had the same failure shape (host-side cache, device-side silence). subs{} is the /crash of pairing: the observability arrives with the second bug.

nodes.norm_label: pins the firmware owns and what writing to them does

nodes.norm_label: boot uses the internal pull-up — v1.22.1
nodes.rationale: The first remote rotation test caught a phantom press — asked 180, landed 90. The 'external 10 K pull-up' the code trusted was an unverified claim in the project's own T4-S3 note; the schematic shows none, so plain INPUT floated. The note is corrected, not quietly edited. (v1.18.0 had credited that pull-up for GPIO0 reading H at rest.)

nodes.label: The Lab: GPIO, I2C scanner, UART monitor — v1.17.0 / v1.18.0 / v1.18.1
nodes.norm_label: the lab: gpio, i2c scanner, uart monitor — v1.17.0 / v1.18.0 / v1.18.1
nodes.rationale: The 14 header pins the firmware does not own (21, 38–42, 47, 48, TX0/RX0, the four SD pins): Hi-Z / pull-up / pull-down / output per pin with live readout; I2C scanner on any two whitelist pins via Wire1 plus a read-only scan of the internal 6/7 bus (PMU, touch controller, P4 plug); UART on Serial1 with a 512-byte tail. Leaving returns every pin to Hi-Z. The whitelist came from the schematic cross-checked against the board config: GPIO18 is on the header and still excluded — it is the display's TE line; on the header ≠ free (D035). First feature shipped entirely over the air. v1.18.0: GPIO0 joins input-only — BOOT is hard-wired to ground, so an output driving high is one press from shorting the pad; apply_mode() refuses it in code because the UI is one edit away from being wrong; bus dropdowns gained a bus_map[] so adding a pin at the front of PINS[] cannot shift every I2C/UART selection by one and scan the wrong pins with no error (D036). v1.18.1: the Back button moved to a bottom bar — it had floated over the UART tab.

nodes.norm_label: bus_map: dropdown position -> pin, built at app entry, excludes input-only pins
nodes.rationale: Selecting bus pins by dropdown position indexed straight into PINS[] would have shifted every bus selection when GPIO0 was inserted first: a scan on the wrong pins with no error, looking like broken hardware.

nodes.norm_label: d035 - the lab may only touch pins the firmware does not own
nodes.rationale: The owner asked for the device to double as a bench tool: set GPIOs, scan I2C, talk serial. The danger is that most pins on this board are spoken for, and one careless write is a corrupted panel or a crashed chip, not an error message. First feature shipped entirely over OTA.

nodes.label: D036 - GPIO0 is readable, never drivable
nodes.norm_label: d036 - gpio0 is readable, never drivable
nodes.rationale: The Lab shipped in v1.17.0 with a 14-pin whitelist that omitted GPIO0. The owner had asked days earlier whether the BOOT button could be a normal button (yes - a strapping pin is only special at reset), then the bench tool that pokes pins did not list it: two true statements adding up to a confusing product. nodes.label: T4-S3
nodes.rationale: Read from BOARD_AMOLED_241 in LilyGo_AMOLED.h and the schematic T4-S3-240719.pdf, not README tables.

nodes.label: Deliberately absent: authentication, rollback, resume
nodes.rationale: Anyone on the LAN can flash the clock - accepted for a desk gadget on a private network; an X-OTA-Token header against an NVS field is trivial to add. The stock Arduino core does not enable CONFIG_BOOTLOADER_APP_ROLLBACK_ENABLE, so a crash-looping image needs the cable: OTA replaces routine flashing, not recovery. Mitigations: pio run must succeed locally before tools/ota pushes; magic-byte check. A failed push is pushed again; Update.abort() resets state.

nodes.label: The Lab pin whitelist
nodes.rationale: Built by cross-referencing the schematic (T4-S3-240719.pdf, header P5) against the library board config - what physically reaches the header minus what the firmware owns. Free: 21, 38, 39, 40, 41, 42, 47, 48. UART0 43/44 (TX0/RX0, the UART tab default). 1-4 shared with the SD socket, fine with no card. GPIO18 is the cautionary tale: on the header and the display's tearing-effect signal - on the header != free.

nodes.label: UART is Serial1, never Serial
nodes.rationale: Serial is the USB console. Any whitelist pin pair via the GPIO matrix; 43/44 default because that is what they are.

nodes.label: bus_map[] instead of an ordering convention on PINS[]
nodes.norm_label: bus_map[] instead of an ordering convention on pins[]
nodes.rationale: The I2C and UART tabs select pins by dropdown position indexed straight into PINS[]; adding an entry at the front would have shifted every selection by one - a scan on the wrong pins with no error. Input-only pins are absent from the bus dropdowns via a bus_map[] built once at app entry; an ordering convention would have broken silently the first time someone inserted a pin mid-array. apply_mode() also refuses PM_OUT on an input-only pin even though the UI cannot request it: the UI is one edit from wrong, the pad short is permanent.

nodes.label: A pin with a button hard-wired to ground must never be an output
nodes.norm_label: a pin with a button hard-wired to ground must never be an output
nodes.rationale: The BOOT button connects GPIO0 to GND permanently: set it to Out, drive high, and one press shorts the pad through nothing but the button, against a pad rated ~40 mA. Supporting reasons: BOOT-at-reset is the only rescue path since there is no OTA rollback (D034); it is still a strapping pin (held low at reset enters USB download mode). The external 10 K pull-up means Hi-Z reads H at rest and L while pressed.
nodes.source_file: docs/decisions/D036 - GPIO0 is readable, never drivable.md

nodes.label: A whitelist of libraries, not the language's own set
nodes.norm_label: a whitelist of libraries, not the language's own set
nodes.rationale: io, os, package and debug are not loaded - each is a way out of the sandbox. GPIO bindings enforce the same pin rules as the Lab, including GPIO0 readable never drivable. Names validated to letters, digits, space, - and _ (no dot or slash) so a name cannot escape /apps/; verified against ?name=../../etc/passwd. No I2C/UART bindings yet; no auth, consistent with /update.

nodes.label: BOOT button (GPIO0): orientation control since v1.22.0, INPUT_PULLUP
nodes.norm_label: boot button (gpio0): orientation control since v1.22.0, input_pullup
nodes.rationale: A strapping pin sampled only at reset, afterwards an ordinary active-low input. Plain INPUT floats and produces phantom presses; an earlier note claimed an external 10K pull-up the schematic does not show. Held during reset it still enters USB download mode, so the flash escape hatch survives; any enclosure must leave it pressable at plug-in.

nodes.label: GPIO18: on the header but owned (display tearing-effect line)
nodes.norm_label: gpio18: on the header but owned (display tearing-effect line)
nodes.rationale: On the header != free. This pin is the reason the Lab whitelist is a written decision and not just an array.

nodes.label: Leave no trace: exit returns every pin to Hi-Z, ends Serial1 and Wire1
nodes.norm_label: leave no trace: exit returns every pin to hi-z, ends serial1 and wire1
nodes.rationale: Launching and leaving the Lab is electrically invisible.

nodes.label: GPIO0 in the Lab with Hi-Z / In PU / In PD and no Out
nodes.norm_label: gpio0 in the lab with hi-z / in pu / in pd and no out
nodes.rationale: The BOOT button is hard-wired from GPIO0 to ground, so an output driving high is one press away from shorting the pad through the button; it is also the flash rescue path with no OTA rollback, and a strapping pin that traps the ROM in download mode if held low across reset. apply_mode() refuses PM_OUT even though the dropdown cannot request it.

nodes.rationale: GPIO18 reaches the header AND is the display TE line: on the header != free. UART monitor replaces unprintable bytes with "." because a lone 0xB7 is invalid UTF-8 and corrupts the label decode after it.

nodes.label: POST /msg, GET /messages, POST /send
nodes.rationale: POST /msg {from, text} delivers; the arrival is announced on the line display through the emotion queue, the one legal door (D018), and a 16-deep inbox feeds the Messages app. GET /messages reads it; POST /send {ip, text} makes this device send, which is also the test seam: curl can play a second gadget in both directions (D039).

nodes.label: HTTP into the existing async server + mDNS-SD discovery
nodes.norm_label: http into the existing async server + mdns-sd discovery
nodes.rationale: The server, mDNS and HTTPClient are already running or linked; delivery is push (the receiver's server takes the POST); identity is a TXT record; it works across APs on one LAN. Rejected: ESP-NOW (identity is a MAC, channel-locked to the AP's channel, no reach across APs, a second radio protocol to coexist with); MQTT (needs a broker, the external dependency the scope boundary exists to forbid); raw UDP (reinvents the discovery and delivery confirmation mDNS + HTTP give for free).

nodes.label: An equalizer for whatever the Mac is playing — v1.39.0
nodes.norm_label: an equalizer for whatever the mac is playing — v1.39.0
nodes.rationale: The clock has no microphone, so the Mac captures its OWN output with ScreenCaptureKit (no virtual-audio driver, no rerouting), runs a 2048-point FFT in Accelerate, and streams 32 log-spaced band levels at 30 fps as one hex line per frame — 2 KB/s. The app draws them theme-colored with gravity peak caps in both orientations. GET /eq reports state; ?demo=1 / EQ_FORCE_DEMO=1 stream a synthetic spectrum, which is how the bars were verified before the audio permission existed. Needs the one-time macOS 'Screen & System Audio Recording' grant for whichever app runs tools/ytserve (D058).

nodes.label: Long-pressing a drawer tile reset the device; the layout is the model — v1.14.0
nodes.norm_label: long-pressing a drawer tile reset the device; the layout is the model — v1.14.0
nodes.rationale: The handler deleted the active screen from inside an event callback on one of that screen's own grandchildren, then rebuilt it — so lv_disp_t.act_scr was left dangling and the first lv_obj_create() of the rebuild invalidated through it. Structural, not a race. Nothing needs deleting: the tiles are flex children, so lv_obj_move_to_index() IS the reorder (D031). The same handler would then have launched the app it had just moved, because LVGL sends LV_EVENT_CLICKED on every release including the end of a long press. Same release retired the 3-second hold (D030) and gave the timer three gestures on one control (D032).

nodes.label: Deleting a screen mid-scroll was a use-after-free — v1.19.1
nodes.norm_label: deleting a screen mid-scroll was a use-after-free — v1.19.1
nodes.rationale: LVGL's obj_del_core() clears act_obj, last_obj and last_pressed when an object dies — but never scroll_obj. Delete a screen while a finger is scrolling on it and the input device keeps a pointer into freed memory, which the scroll-throw handler dereferences on the next read. release_input() now runs before every screen deletion. Found because the drawer could not show five apps (678 px of tiles in a 600 px row) and now wraps and scrolls vertically only, so it cannot fight the left-edge back gesture. Also: a drag in the drawer launched an app (LV_EVENT_CLICKED fires on any press-release), and script uploads rebuilt the registry from the web server's task, racing app_at() on the LVGL task — uploads now mark it dirty and the rebuild happens on the LVGL task.

nodes.label: tools/eq_capture (Swift): ScreenCaptureKit capture + Accelerate FFT
nodes.rationale: ScreenCaptureKit with capturesAudio, the path OBS takes on modern macOS: no virtual-audio driver, no rerouting the owner's sound, nothing installed; Chrome, Music, a video in Safari, all of it because it is the system mix. DSP in Accelerate: Hann window, 2048-point real FFT at 48 kHz, 32 log-spaced bands from 40 Hz to 16 kHz, peak-in-band in dB, a slow AGC that makes the running peak full scale so a quiet podcast fills the bars like a loud track, attack 0.60 / decay 0.14 per frame. Output: one line of 64 hex characters per frame at 30 fps, 2 KB/s. ScreenCaptureKit needs the one-time macOS grant 'Screen & System Audio Recording' for whichever app launched the helper; the helper reports '!grant ...' and that status travels the whole path to the panel. The helper also reports its audio format and a level line every ten seconds so the next silence is diagnosable from the companion log alone (verified: Float32 non-interleaved at 48 kHz).

nodes.label: Piecewise-linear resting LiPo voltage-to-percent curve
nodes.rationale: The SY6970 is a charger, not a fuel gauge: no coulomb counter, only the cell voltage from its ADC (SY.enableMeasure() already called by beginAMOLED_241). Percent is derived through 4.20 V -> 100 %, 3.82 V -> 50 %, 3.45 V -> 0 %, and the display is honest: it reads low under load and high on the charger (the CV phase holds 4.2 V long before full, so the chip turns green while charging to say 'this is a charger number'), and it moves in steps, sampled every 30 s. A proper gauge IC is a hardware change and out of scope. Superseded in part by D044, where voltage becomes the tether rather than the gauge.

nodes.label: Hybrid gauge (gauge.cpp): coulombs while charging, model while discharging
nodes.norm_label: hybrid gauge (gauge.cpp): coulombs while charging, model while discharging
nodes.rationale: The owner asked for a real coulomb counter, but the SY6970 register map settles it: it measures charge current (REG 0x12, 50 mA steps) and has no discharge-current ADC and no accumulator, so nothing in the silicon can see current leaving the battery. Charging integrates measured current (genuine coulombs); charge-complete snaps to 100 %, the one absolute anchor; discharging integrates a modelled draw (88 mA base + 82 mA x brightness/255) tethered to the voltage curve with a ~50 min time constant, so error cannot accumulate past what the curve allows while the reading stays smooth and monotonic. State persists in NVS (at most one write a minute, normally on a >=1 % change); a stored value more than 25 points from the curve at boot is discarded. settings.batt_mah (default 5000) scales the arithmetic; /health reports gauge:'hybrid', signed ma, and mah_used.

nodes.label: 'weather 496370 h ago' — v1.10.1
nodes.rationale: 496370 h is 56.6 years — the age of the Unix epoch, exactly now / 3600. Weather and NTP both start on GOT_IP and race; weather usually wins, so the fetch was stamped with a near-zero epoch, and when NTP stepped the clock to 2026 the age measured the distance back to 1970. Age is now measured with millis(), which cannot be stepped, and uint32 subtraction wraps correctly at the ~49.7-day rollover. All three call sites — tap overlay, GET /health, Settings ▸ Info — go through one net_weather_age_s() accessor so the bug cannot be reintroduced in one place while being fixed in another.

nodes.norm_label: fliqlo_digits — a 210 px, ten-glyph lvgl font generated with lv_font_conv
nodes.rationale: npx lv_font_conv --font 'Arial Bold.ttf' --size 210 --bpp 4 --range 0x30-0x39 --no-kerning --no-compress -o src/fliqlo_digits.c. Subsetting to ten glyphs is what keeps a 210 px font affordable: ~90 KB of 4 bpp bitmap data. Metrics: adv_w 1869/16 = 116.8 px for all ten digits, box_h 148–153, line_height 154, base_line 3. Arial Bold is the closest bold neo-grotesque to Fliqlo's numerals already on macOS as a plain .ttf (Helvetica ships as a .ttc, which lv_font_conv handles less reliably). Licensing: Arial is a Monotype face — fine for a personal device, but if published swap in Inter, Roboto or Archivo by re-running the one command; nothing else in the code refers to the typeface.

nodes.label: D011 - Generate the digit font, do not scale Montserrat
nodes.norm_label: d011 - generate the digit font, do not scale montserrat
nodes.rationale: Fliqlo digits need ~150 px on a 450 px panel; LVGL 8's bundled Montserrat stops at 48 px and an lv_label cannot be scaled. Options: scale a 48 px label via lv_img transform (labels aren't images — render-to-canvas per frame, blurry and expensive); ten pre-rendered A8 images (~470 KB, loses text layout); or generate a real LVGL font, digits only — chosen. nodes.label: D012 - Card geometry
nodes.rationale: All numbers fall out of the one font metric from D011 — 116.8 px per digit, 233.6 px per two-digit card. Clock row y = 44, height 232; weather row TOP_MID at y 302 as a flex row with LV_FLEX_ALIGN_END so the 48 px temperature and 28 px min/max share a bottom edge without a hand-tuned nudge. Type sizes: digits 210, temperature 48, min/max 28 — exactly the brief's cap of two sizes besides the digits. Frontmatter: id D012, 2026-08-16, accepted, origin Stage 1, tags decision/layout.

nodes.label: ESP32-S3 shares one 2.4 GHz radio between Wi-Fi and BLE
nodes.norm_label: esp32-s3 shares one 2.4 ghz radio between wi-fi and ble
nodes.rationale: The ESP32-S3 has one radio; Wi-Fi and BLE share it through a coexistence layer that is unforgiving, which is the root cause of both boot-loop crashes.

nodes.label: Boot order
nodes.rationale: Serial -> settings_load() -> beginAMOLED_241() -> setRotation() -> beginLvglHelper() -> ui_init() -> emotion_begin() -> ble_begin() BEFORE Wi-Fi -> net_begin(); httpapi starts on first association.

nodes.label: Main loop: lv_timer_handler -> emotion_tick -> app_host_tick

nodes.label: D017 - BLE and Wi-Fi coexistence
nodes.rationale: Owner asked for BLE, reversing the brief's 'v1 is Wi-Fi only'. Recorded as a deliberate change of direction, not drift. Enabling BLE plus the async HTTP server cost 22.8%->26.9% flash and 15.5%->18.1% RAM, judged comfortable.

nodes.label: Module map
nodes.rationale: Twenty-four source files, ~9000 lines: what each owns and what it may not do, organised around the one unbroken rule that only the LVGL task draws.

nodes.label: Decode the backtrace, do not guess
nodes.norm_label: decode the backtrace, do not guess
nodes.rationale: Both coexistence crashes were solved by decoding the backtrace with xtensa-esp32s3-elf-addr2line; monitor_filters = esp32_exception_decoder does it automatically in pio device monitor. Reach for it first on any abort.

nodes.label: BLE must start before Wi-Fi (ble_begin before net_begin)
nodes.norm_label: ble must start before wi-fi (ble_begin before net_begin)
nodes.rationale: NimBLEDevice::init() brings up radio coexistence; if Wi-Fi has already claimed the radio, coex_core_enable aborts and the device boot-loops forever. ble_begin() is therefore called before net_begin() in setup(). Called the single most fragile ordering in the firmware.

nodes.label: NimBLE over Bluedroid
nodes.rationale: NimBLE is roughly a third of the flash and RAM of Bluedroid for a peripheral-only role. Pinned h2zero/NimBLE-Arduino ^1.4.2 because 2.x requires ESP32 core 3.x and the project is on 2.0.17 via espressif32@6.12.0.

nodes.label: Wi-Fi modem sleep is mandatory once Bluetooth is enabled
nodes.norm_label: wi-fi modem sleep is mandatory once bluetooth is enabled
nodes.rationale: net_begin() had WiFi.setSleep(false) for lower HTTP latency, which is illegal once BT is enabled: modem sleep is how Wi-Fi yields airtime to Bluetooth, and without it the Wi-Fi task aborts. Now WiFi.setSleep(ble_is_running()), toggled at runtime by ble_begin()/ble_stop(). Accepted cost: tens of ms of HTTP latency, invisible for an occasional emotion POST.

nodes.label: Add the diagnostic before rewriting
nodes.rationale: A single Serial.printf reporting what the overlay actually created ('eyes=yes seam=on digits=dimmed msg=yes') settled 'broken or invisible?' in one flash cycle. Two project bugs have been design failures presenting as code failures - this one and the invisible 5-second hold in the Settings screen.

nodes.label: Two boot loops from radio coexistence, diagnosed from decoded backtraces
nodes.norm_label: two boot loops from radio coexistence, diagnosed from decoded backtraces
nodes.rationale: abort() in coex_core_enable <- esp_bt_controller_enable <- NimBLEDevice::init: BLE must init before Wi-Fi claims the one 2.4 GHz radio. And WiFi.setSleep(false) is illegal once BT is on because modem sleep is how Wi-Fi yields airtime; now conditional on ble_is_running().

nodes.label: BLE Nordic UART Service transport
nodes.rationale: Service 6E400001-B5A3-F393-E0A9-E50E24DCCA9E, RX 6E400002 (write JSON), TX 6E400003 (notify ok/err), so any generic BLE tool works; device name in Settings ▸ BLE (default FlipClock). With Pairable on, the device advertises a HID service — the only thing that lists it in macOS Bluetooth settings — under a custom vendor-defined 'desktop gadget' identity, not a keyboard, so Keyboard Setup Assistant does not appear (D022); 'Identify as keyboard' is the compatible fallback. Hosts cache the HID descriptor per bond: after changing that switch, forget the device on the host, Clear pairings on the clock, pair again. BLE from the Mac needs pip install bleak and macOS Bluetooth permission — a process without it is killed with SIGABRT, not given an error.

nodes.norm_label: two-phase split-flap fold (180 ms per phase, lv_anim height animations)
nodes.rationale: Phase 1: the old top half shrinks revealing the new top while a static cover keeps the old bottom visible; phase 2: the new bottom grows from the seam. Panels delete themselves via lv_anim_set_ready_cb; the seam is moved to the foreground after each flap.

nodes.norm_label: tearing: a single full-screen psram buffer composites the whole frame; te (gpio18) unused by the stock flush path

nodes.label: D009 - LVGL buffer strategy
nodes.rationale: Use beginLvglHelper() — one full-screen 600×450×2 = 527 KB buffer in PSRAM via ps_malloc, flushed with pushColors — rather than beginLvglHelperDMA() (2 × 1/10-screen ≈ 108 KB in internal SRAM via MALLOC_CAP_DMA). Revisit only if the flip visibly stutters at Stage 2, and then by reducing the animated area, not by switching to the DMA helper. Frontmatter: id D009, 2026-08-16, accepted, origin analysis, tags decision/lvgl/memory.

nodes.label: D015 - Abu Dhabi locale
nodes.rationale: The owner is in Abu Dhabi. Defaults: city Abu Dhabi, latitude 24.4539, longitude 54.3773, POSIX TZ <+04>-4. Verified against system tzdata rather than assumed: UTC+4 with no DST in either direction (January and July both +04), so the string carries no changeover rules. All DST handling is delegated to libc via setenv("TZ") + tzset(); the firmware never computes a daylight-saving transition, which also makes the European and US entries in the timezone table correct for free. Frontmatter: id D015, 2026-08-16, accepted, origin owner, tags decision/time.

nodes.label: Every build flag is load-bearing
nodes.rationale: -DBOARD_HAS_PSRAM: without it LilyGo_AMOLED.h raises #error 'Detected that PSRAM is not turned on'. memory_type qio_opi: without it the 8 MB OPI PSRAM is not mapped and ps_malloc of the 527 KB LVGL buffer fails. -DARDUINO_USB_CDC_ON_BOOT=1: no serial output over native USB. -DLV_CONF_INCLUDE_SIMPLE: LVGL cannot find lv_conf.h. -DLILYGO_TDISPLAY_AMOLED_SERIES: board-family guard inside the library. None of these is stylistic.

nodes.label: Single full-screen framebuffer in PSRAM
nodes.rationale: The brief requires framebuffers in PSRAM, and MALLOC_CAP_DMA on the ESP32-S3 cannot be satisfied from OPI PSRAM. Internal SRAM is the scarce resource — 320 KB total, spent on the Wi-Fi stack, ESPAsyncWebServer, mDNS and three FreeRTOS task stacks — so handing 108 KB of it to display buffers for a clock that redraws twice a minute is the wrong trade when 8 MB of PSRAM is available. A single full-screen buffer is also the anti-tearing configuration for the split-flap: the whole frame is flushed in one pushColors call, so the panel never shows half of frame n and half of n+1. Accepted cost: ~540 KB over a 36 MHz QSPI bus (≈18 MB/s) is ~30 ms minimum per full flush — a ceiling around 30 fps, comfortably enough for a ~400 ms flip that only dirties the two card rectangles.

nodes.label: POSIX TZ string <+04>-4 — two things that look like typos and are not
nodes.norm_label: posix tz string <+04>-4 — two things that look like typos and are not
nodes.rationale: The angle brackets are required: POSIX TZ wants a name for the zone abbreviation, and since 2017 the IANA database emits numeric abbreviations instead of inventing ones like GST; a bare +04 is not parseable as a name. The offset sign is inverted: -4 means UTC+4, because POSIX defines the field as the value added to local time to reach UTC — getting it backwards puts the clock 8 hours out, the single most common POSIX TZ mistake. tail -c 60 /usr/share/zoneinfo/Asia/Dubai emits exactly <+04>-4; the string is copied from tzdata, not composed by hand.

nodes.label: Flip driven by "rendered digit differs from target", per card
nodes.norm_label: flip driven by "rendered digit differs from target", per card
nodes.rationale: Never arithmetic on the previous value: 23:59 -> 00:00 changes both cards and the hour goes 23 -> 00, and the first post-NTP jump animates correctly instead of desyncing.

nodes.label: First paint after NTP does not animate (animate = last_min >= 0)
nodes.norm_label: first paint after ntp does not animate (animate = last_min >= 0)
nodes.rationale: Otherwise the device would fold dramatically from a meaningless 00:00 to the real time on every boot.

nodes.label: Anti burn-in: slow random walk within +/-2 px applied to the layout root
nodes.norm_label: anti burn-in: slow random walk within +/-2 px applied to the layout root
nodes.rationale: +/-1 px per step every BURNIN_STEP_SECONDS (180), bounded to +/-2 px: a walk, not a jump, so it is never perceptible. Prefer even offsets so the rounder does not enlarge redraw regions; card geometry leaves >= 2 px margin so it never clips. The pure-black background is already most of the defence; the walk protects digits and card edges. Toggleable in Settings.

nodes.label: Stock LVGL keyboard with no textarea: keys go to the host
nodes.norm_label: stock lvgl keyboard with no textarea: keys go to the host
nodes.rationale: kb_cb translates button text through an ASCII->usage table; arrows, backspace and enter map to their usage codes; mode keys stay local. ble_key() sends press and release as one call so a stuck modifier on the host cannot depend on a second call happening. A dim 24-char tail shows what was typed as feedback only; nothing is stored. No six-key rollover or held modifiers beyond shift (a message-typing keyboard, not a gaming one); non-US host layouts render some symbols differently because usage codes name positions, not glyphs.

nodes.label: app_touch_count() reads the CST226's raw point count
nodes.norm_label: app_touch_count() reads the cst226's raw point count
nodes.rationale: Two fingers are the one thing LVGL cannot see: its pointer indev reports only the first touch. app_touch_count() reads the controller's raw point count while a press is live, double-reading the controller the LVGL helper also polls; watched for, accepted, and hardware-verified by the owner (the count is read-only state, not a cleared FIFO). D056 extends it to app_touch_points().

nodes.label: Laptop-pad gesture set
nodes.rationale: One finger moves the cursor (gain 1.5, fractional carry); a still tap under 250 ms is a left click; a two-finger tap is a right click; a two-finger drag is the scroll wheel; strip buttons give explicit Left/Right for drag-free clicking. A click is two reports (down, then up ~30 ms later on the app's tick) and destroy() always sends an all-up report: leaving a phantom held button on the host is the one unforgivable trackpad bug. The app owns its screen, so its gestures are its own business (D027).

nodes.label: clip_corner set on the card for the fold
nodes.norm_label: clip_corner set on the card for the fold
nodes.rationale: Set at Stage 1, needed at Stage 2: when the fold animation moves a digit copy past the card edge, clipping keeps it inside the rounded rectangle instead of spilling onto the black background.

nodes.label: The seam is scale-dependent, not all-or-nothing
nodes.norm_label: the seam is scale-dependent, not all-or-nothing
nodes.rationale: The seam draws OVER the numerals — in Fliqlo the split line crosses the glyphs because it is the gap between two physical flaps — so make_card() creates it after the label. It reads correctly at 232 px, where 3 px is a hairline; it does not survive being scaled: on the 55 px corner clock and 58 px weather cards there are too few pixels for a line to land on and it reads as choppy. Big cards keep it, small cards have none (v1.4.1 removed it everywhere, v1.4.2 restored it where it works). The fold never depended on it — it hinges at CARD_H/2.

nodes.label: Seam rule becomes scale-dependent — v1.4.1 / v1.4.2 / v1.4.3
nodes.norm_label: seam rule becomes scale-dependent — v1.4.1 / v1.4.2 / v1.4.3
nodes.rationale: v1.4.1 removed the seam from every card: once the same card language was applied at 55 and 58 px as well as 232 px, a 2 px line across a 55 px card has too few pixels to sit cleanly and reads as choppy. v1.4.2 restored it on the big clock only, thinner (3 → 2 px): at 232 px a hairline says split-flap; what it does not survive is being scaled. v1.4.3 settled on 3 px for the big clock, none on small cards. The fold animation never depended on it — it hinges at CARD_H/2 regardless. The v1.4.1 release also removed the per-card accent object, dead since the v4 line renderer stopped pulsing it.

nodes.label: First-boot sentinel key silences Preferences' NOT_FOUND noise
nodes.norm_label: first-boot sentinel key silences preferences' not_found noise
nodes.rationale: Opening the namespace read-only on a virgin device logged nvs_open failed: NOT_FOUND; opening read-write exposed worse — Arduino's Preferences logs ESP_LOGE for every absent key even when a default is supplied, six red lines on a perfectly healthy boot. Error-level noise on a healthy path is not cosmetic: a log you have learned to ignore has stopped being a log. Fix: probe one sentinel key (tz); absent → first boot, seed NVS from the defaults and return without reading; present → every read is silent. Verified: both a virgin boot and a seeded boot produce zero error lines.

nodes.label: NVS reads guarded by isKey() with a one-shot backfill; first-boot sentinel seeding
nodes.norm_label: nvs reads guarded by iskey() with a one-shot backfill; first-boot sentinel seeding
nodes.rationale: Arduino Preferences logs an error for every absent key even with a default; six red herrings on a healthy boot hide a real fault later. Adding a setting in a newer firmware is now a non-event (blen, bkbd picked up silently).

nodes.label: Settings navigates like Apple's and nothing in it scrolls sideways — v1.26.0 / v1.27.1–v1.27.3
nodes.norm_label: settings navigates like apple's and nothing in it scrolls sideways — v1.26.0 / v1.27.1–v1.27.3
nodes.rationale: The tabview is gone: landscape shows a macOS-style sidebar (section list + pane), portrait an iOS-style stack (tap pushes the page, back pops it); everything scrolls vertically so nothing competes with the left-edge back swipe (D048). Eleven fixed widths from the 600-wide tabview era were living inside D048's 410 px pane and helper labels sized to their text, so text sailed off the right edge — every width is now percentage-of-pane and every helper label wraps. LVGL containers are scrollable by default, so a flex row wider than the pane scrolls HORIZONTALLY rather than wrapping; all row containers now wrap, size to content and have SCROLLABLE cleared. Four row rules (D048 addendum): one setting per row; label left, control right; sliders get label + live value above a full-width bar; groups titled by section headers — implemented as helpers setting_row and slider_row, orientation-proof by construction.

nodes.label: Settings row rules: setting_row / row_control / slider_row / section
nodes.norm_label: settings row rules: setting_row / row_control / slider_row / section
nodes.rationale: The Screen page proved that wrap is a fallback, not a layout. Four rules: one setting per row (full-width, card-coloured, fixed height); label left-centre, its one control right-centre (a row that would need to wrap is two settings); a slider is the tall variant (label top-left, live value top-right, slider full-width beneath); groups get a section() header and nothing else. The same rows serve both orientations untouched, because full-width-plus-one-control cannot overflow either pane. Screen is converted; other pages adopt the helpers as they are next touched (v1.27.3).

nodes.norm_label: battery gauge counts coulombs where measurable — v1.23.0
nodes.rationale: The SY6970 measures charge current but cannot see discharge current, so charging integrates the measured mA (real coulomb counting), charge-done snaps to 100 %, and discharge integrates a brightness-aware model tethered to the voltage curve (~50 min time constant) so error cannot accumulate. State survives reboot via NVS; batt_mah (default 5000) scales it; /health gains gauge, signed ma, mah_used. Also fixes the chip showing green on a full battery: the library's isCharging() counts DONE as charging and isChargeDone() returns the opposite of its name. A true counter remains a ~3 € INA226 on the Lab's I2C pins; gauge_update() is the seam where it would slot in.

nodes.norm_label: d028 - set a number by dragging the number
nodes.rationale: The timer shipped in v1.11.0 with one drag target (the whole face); seconds were unreachable. The owner asked for the 'Night from' layout for every number while keeping the flip-card design. Night from is a roller not because rollers are good but because it gives one control per number - so each card becomes its own roller.

nodes.label: D029 - Back is a system gesture, not a widget event
nodes.norm_label: d029 - back is a system gesture, not a widget event
nodes.rationale: Every app needs a way home; a Clock button per app is a rule each new app must remember. The owner asked for the phone gesture: swipe in from the left edge. An event handler on the app screen cannot work because LVGL 8 does not bubble events - any clickable child eats the press. Destination later revised by D033 (one level, not home); the mechanism stands.
nodes.source_file: docs/decisions/D029 - Back is a system gesture, not a widget event.md

nodes.label: D030 - Retire the 3-second hold
nodes.rationale: The 3 s hold opened Settings when Settings was the only other screen. Once Settings became an app reached through the drawer (D026), the hold was a second route to a place that already had one. D027 warned every gesture makes the next harder; the first to go is the one whose reason expired.

nodes.label: D032 - Three gestures, one control
nodes.rationale: The v1.12.0 roller cards (D028) were still 'tricky': at 13 px a step on a 450 px screen a full drag is 34 steps, so 45 seconds took two drags and an exact landing a third, while a 220 ms fold lagged the finger. Faster drag fixes range and worsens aim - opposite problems one control cannot solve.

nodes.label: D033 - Back goes one level, not home
nodes.norm_label: d033 - back goes one level, not home
nodes.rationale: The left-edge swipe (D029) jumped straight to the clock. With a drawer between the clock and a growing set of apps that stopped matching the path the user walked (leave the timer to open Settings and you were thrown past the drawer). The owner asked for the stack model plus visible back buttons; the timer had none after v1.14.0 removed its Clock button.
nodes.source_file: docs/decisions/D033 - Back goes one level, not home.md

nodes.label: The clock is not an app
nodes.norm_label: the clock is not an app
nodes.rationale: The clock is the resting state of the object; the drawer is a layer above it. Apps are a platform, not special cases, and the clock sits beneath that platform rather than inside it — see Module map for what every file owns.

nodes.label: Dedicated full-screen text editor overlay
nodes.rationale: Chosen over shrinking the tab or scrolling the field into view because: the field can never be occluded (fixed, known position); one entry point (LV_EVENT_CLICKED opens it, no hidden/shown state to get stuck in); explicit Done/Cancel so committing is a decision; room for a 24 px font. Passwords default to visible in the editor with a Hide checkbox; the settings-tab field stays masked (D016).
nodes.source_file: docs/decisions/D019 - Text entry gets its own screen.md

nodes.label: A drawer rather than double-tap
nodes.rationale: Double-tap addresses one app; a drawer addresses all of them, and leaves the gesture budget intact (D027). The owner replaced the double-tap idea before any code existed.
nodes.source_file: docs/decisions/D026 - Apps are a platform, not a special case.md

nodes.label: The clock is not an app: it is the resting state
nodes.norm_label: the clock is not an app: it is the resting state
nodes.rationale: Every decision has pushed the same way - true black so pixels are off, animations that revert on their own, a display that clears when work stops. Demoting the clock to a tile would contradict all of it. Home is the clock, the drawer is a layer above it, apps are screens the drawer launches, everything returns home on its own.
nodes.source_file: docs/decisions/D026 - Apps are a platform, not a special case.md

nodes.label: Inside apps there is no budget problem
nodes.norm_label: inside apps there is no budget problem
nodes.rationale: An app owns its own screen, so it owns its own gestures and can use real buttons with real labels. Only the home screen is constrained, because only the home screen has to stay empty.

nodes.label: The gesture budget: every gesture makes the next one harder
nodes.norm_label: the gesture budget: every gesture makes the next one harder
nodes.rationale: Four gestures is close to the limit for a screen with no affordances. A fifth should be resisted unless shown disjoint from all four; the honest alternative is a button inside an app where there is room for a label.

nodes.label: Three rules keep the bottom swipe disjoint from press gestures
nodes.norm_label: three rules keep the bottom swipe disjoint from press gestures
nodes.rationale: A swipe begins as a press, so naively it also registers as a tap or worse a brightness-changing long press. Rules: displacement > ~30 px disqualifies a press whatever its duration; the swipe must start at the bottom edge (y > height - 80), keeping the rest of the screen free; suppress the hold indicator once movement starts.

nodes.label: The value is absolute, not accumulated
nodes.norm_label: the value is absolute, not accumulated
nodes.rationale: Each PRESSING event recomputes from total displacement since PRESSED ((drag_y0 - y) / PX_PER_STEP) rather than adding a delta. Accumulating drifts and makes the gesture irreversible; absolute means returning your finger to where it started returns the number exactly.

nodes.label: The card keeps LV_OBJ_FLAG_CLICKABLE
nodes.rationale: It is the control, so it is the one object on the screen that must NOT be passed to decor() (D014).
nodes.source_file: docs/decisions/D028 - Set a number by dragging the number.md

nodes.label: flip_to() is a deliberate second copy of the clock's split flap
nodes.norm_label: flip_to() is a deliberate second copy of the clock's split flap
nodes.rationale: Extracting the original would mean refactoring the one screen that has worked all day to add a feature elsewhere; a short duplicate is the cheaper risk today. If a third caller appears, extract it then - two is not yet a pattern.
nodes.source_file: docs/decisions/D028 - Set a number by dragging the number.md

nodes.label: Each card is its own roller: the thing you drag is the thing that displays it
nodes.norm_label: each card is its own roller: the thing you drag is the thing that displays it
nodes.rationale: Minutes card sets minutes, seconds card sets seconds; which number you are changing is unambiguous because you are touching it. The timer stops looking like a different app - it is the same object as the clock doing something else.
nodes.source_file: docs/decisions/D028 - Set a number by dragging the number.md

nodes.label: A fold in progress is not queued behind
nodes.norm_label: a fold in progress is not queued behind
nodes.rationale: Dragging generates changes far faster than a 220 ms fold completes. A folding card takes the new value immediately and animates the next transition; stacked folds render as tearing.
nodes.source_file: docs/decisions/D028 - Set a number by dragging the number.md

nodes.label: indev->proc.state is read directly
nodes.rationale: LVGL 8 has no lv_indev_get_state(); one field from a public struct. A place to check if LVGL is ever unpinned from 8.4.0 (D002).
nodes.source_file: docs/decisions/D029 - Back is a system gesture, not a widget event.md

nodes.label: Judge the last point seen while pressed, not the point read after release
nodes.norm_label: judge the last point seen while pressed, not the point read after release
nodes.rationale: Reading after release trusts the touch driver to leave valid coordinates behind; a driver that zeroes the point would make the gesture silently impossible.
nodes.source_file: docs/decisions/D029 - Back is a system gesture, not a widget event.md

nodes.label: The back gesture is polled from the LVGL loop, above the widget tree
nodes.norm_label: the back gesture is polled from the lvgl loop, above the widget tree
nodes.rationale: Polled in app_host_tick(), not an event handler anywhere: apps get it for free, no app can swallow it, and it is one fewer contract rule that depends on an author remembering something. Mirrors the clock's swipe-up: armed by start within 44 px of the left edge, judged on release (>= 110 px rightward, <= 90 px vertical wander). Two comparisons per frame when nothing is open.
nodes.source_file: docs/decisions/D029 - Back is a system gesture, not a widget event.md

nodes.label: The timer roller abandons a drag that turns mostly sideways and restores the value
nodes.norm_label: the timer roller abandons a drag that turns mostly sideways and restores the value
nodes.rationale: The minutes card spans x = 14..282 and overlaps the edge zone; a back swipe starting on it would drag the roller a few steps, and set_seconds is a static that outlives the screen. Vertical control, vertical input - a better roller independently of the gesture.
nodes.source_file: docs/decisions/D029 - Back is a system gesture, not a widget event.md

nodes.label: Remove the hold and the accent bar that advertised it
nodes.norm_label: remove the hold and the accent bar that advertised it
nodes.rationale: The press path is simpler - nothing happens during a press any more; brightness is decided on release by duration; the PRESSING branch only watches for movement; settings_fired is gone. Resting a finger on the clock no longer opens anything, which was the real cost. Settings is one tap further away, the right distance for a screen visited rarely. Frees budget for the back gesture (D029).

nodes.label: Controls are cards without a seam; no frame around a running number
nodes.norm_label: controls are cards without a seam; no frame around a running number
nodes.rationale: Same charcoal, radius and width, directly under the numbers they act on, but no seam: that line means 'this flips' and through a word reads as a strikethrough. A coloured border around a running number reads as an error box; the Pause label and moving digits already show the state twice.

nodes.label: A thin dim bar at the left edge says the edge is live
nodes.norm_label: a thin dim bar at the left edge says the edge is live
nodes.rationale: The Clock button is gone so the left-edge swipe is the only way out of the timer; a gesture with no affordance is a gesture nobody finds. Same trick the clock used for the hold, now retired (D030).

nodes.label: The timer fold runs at 70 ms a phase, not the clock's 180
nodes.norm_label: the timer fold runs at 70 ms a phase, not the clock's 180
nodes.rationale: The clock folds once a minute and the fold is the point; here it fires on every drag step, and an animation slower than the finger made the number feel like it lagged the intent.

nodes.label: Seconds wrap, minutes clamp
nodes.rationale: Wrapping puts 59 one tap from 0 in either direction; stays reversible during a drag because the value is recomputed from total displacement (D028).

nodes.label: Drag (coarse, 18 px/step), tap above/below middle (+-1), hold (+-1 repeating ~10/s)
nodes.norm_label: drag (coarse, 18 px/step), tap above/below middle (+-1), hold (+-1 repeating ~10/s)
nodes.rationale: Each gesture does what it is good at; the drag can be calmer (13 -> 18 px) because it is no longer the only way to hit a value, and hold-repeat covers all seconds in about six seconds. Above the card's middle is up, below is down - nothing to aim at. drag_moved gates the tap and repeat so a drag never also counts as a tap. Allowed by D027: an app owns its screen, so it owns its gestures.

nodes.label: Back pops one level of the stack the user walked: app -> drawer -> clock
nodes.norm_label: back pops one level of the stack the user walked: app -> drawer -> clock
nodes.rationale: Leaving an app lands where you launched it from and one more swipe reaches the clock. The app-first-refusal hook is unchanged. Supersedes the destination half of D029; the architecture half stands.
nodes.source_file: docs/decisions/D033 - Back goes one level, not home.md

nodes.label: Documented before implementation
nodes.rationale: The restructure is the substance of the request; a timer bolted onto ui.cpp would have satisfied the letter of it and none of the point.

nodes.label: Hold progress bar affordance (appears at 1.2 s, fills at the trigger)
nodes.norm_label: hold progress bar affordance (appears at 1.2 s, fills at the trigger)
nodes.rationale: A silent hold is an invisible affordance: nobody discovers a gesture with no feedback, they let go early and conclude it is broken. Doubles as the brightness-cycle indicator; hidden the instant the finger lifts.

nodes.label: v1.11.0: app_api.h (five fields then), app_host.cpp owns registry, drawer, launch and the route home; adding an app is one file in src/apps/ and one line in the registry; the timer reuses the clock's cards and 210 px digits
nodes.norm_label: v1.11.0: app_api.h (five fields then), app_host.cpp owns registry, drawer, launch and the route home; adding an app is one file in src/apps/ and one line in the registry; the timer reuses the clock's cards and 210 px digits
nodes.rationale: The host never learns what an app draws and no app learns anything about the clock; a second visual language on one device would be one too many.

nodes.label: Displacement disqualifies a press regardless of duration; the swipe must start within 80 px of the bottom
nodes.norm_label: displacement disqualifies a press regardless of duration; the swipe must start within 80 px of the bottom
nodes.rationale: A swipe begins as a press, so without the rule an upward drag also fires a tap, or a long press that silently changes brightness on the way to the drawer.

nodes.label: Left-edge back swipe polled from app_host_tick() above the widget tree; app_host_back() owns what back means (app -> drawer -> clock)
nodes.norm_label: left-edge back swipe polled from app_host_tick() above the widget tree; app_host_back() owns what back means (app -> drawer -> clock)
nodes.rationale: LVGL 8 does not bubble events, so a handler on the app screen would fail on precisely the widgets you are touching. Judge the last point seen while pressed, not the point read after release. The optional App.back() hook lets Settings close its editor and keep a typed password instead of leaving. The drawer is rebuilt on every visit so it can never be stale.

nodes.label: LVGL 8: every object is CLICKABLE, SCROLLABLE and SCROLL_CHAIN by default and events do not bubble
nodes.norm_label: lvgl 8: every object is clickable, scrollable and scroll_chain by default and events do not bubble
nodes.rationale: lv_obj_constructor sets the flags unconditionally; decorative objects swallow presses so a gesture works only in the margins. decor() strips them; lv_scr_act() is an object too and was the last stop on the scroll chain that let the clock be dragged.

nodes.label: v1.14.0: the 3-second hold is gone; Settings is an app and the drawer goes there; nothing happens during a press any more
nodes.norm_label: v1.14.0: the 3-second hold is gone; settings is an app and the drawer goes there; nothing happens during a press any more
nodes.rationale: D027 said every gesture makes the next one harder; the honest first one to spend is the one whose reason expired.

nodes.label: Rotate in place (v1.24.1): remember what was open, tear it down through the host's own paths, rotate, rebuild the clock, relaunch the same app
nodes.norm_label: rotate in place (v1.24.1): remember what was open, tear it down through the host's own paths, rotate, rebuild the clock, relaunch the same app
nodes.rationale: The "go home first" policy was an inference the owner's hands refuted: being thrown home reads as a crash. Create-on-entry apps already know how to be born into any shape, so rotation-in-place costs nothing. Stated casualty: rotating inside Settings discards unsaved edits.

nodes.label: Save / Close split with a snapshot-based unsaved-changes guard; sliders preview only; lv_msgbox_close_async
nodes.norm_label: save / close split with a snapshot-based unsaved-changes guard; sliders preview only; lv_msgbox_close_async
nodes.rationale: Live-previewing sliders meant leaving had already changed the device permanently with no cancel. Discard restores the snapshot; explicit apply-now actions take a fresh one so they never read as unsaved. Deleting an object from inside its own event callback is an LVGL foot-gun.

nodes.label: Settings never scrolls sideways: macOS sidebar in landscape, iOS stack in portrait; rows ROW_WRAP, LV_SIZE_CONTENT tall, SCROLLABLE cleared; one setting per row, label left, control right
nodes.norm_label: settings never scrolls sideways: macos sidebar in landscape, ios stack in portrait; rows row_wrap, lv_size_content tall, scrollable cleared; one setting per row, label left, control right
nodes.rationale: LVGL containers are scrollable by default in every direction: "do not scroll sideways" is a flag to CLEAR on every container that could be too wide, not a rule to follow. Replacing the tabview deleted the gesture conflict with the left-edge back swipe. Widths are percentage-of-pane and the only direction anything grows is down.

nodes.label: State cleared by a common path that one caller needed preserved (Settings edits at rotation, the theme rebuild, the cart picker)
nodes.norm_label: state cleared by a common path that one caller needed preserved (settings edits at rotation, the theme rebuild, the cart picker)
nodes.rationale: Third occurrence in one day; when a report survives the first fix, re-read it literally.

nodes.label: Themes (v1.27.0): the look is a table that builders read; applying a theme is rotate-in-place minus the rotate (app_request_rebuild)
nodes.norm_label: themes (v1.27.0): the look is a table that builders read; applying a theme is rotate-in-place minus the rotate (app_request_rebuild)
nodes.rationale: Because every screen is create-on-entry, theme.cpp is 40 lines and the cascade is a dozen one-line colour reads where cards are born. Background stays true black in every theme (AMOLED; the burn-in walk was tuned against black). The generative-pixel reference is a screen, not a palette. /theme riding app_request_rotation(current) would never have fired because the rotation service skips no-ops.

nodes.label: Timer: each card is its own roller (one control per number); value from total displacement since touch-down; drag coarse at 18 px, tap +/-1, hold repeats; 70 ms fold
nodes.norm_label: timer: each card is its own roller (one control per number); value from total displacement since touch-down; drag coarse at 18 px, tap +/-1, hold repeats; 70 ms fold
nodes.rationale: Night-from is a roller because it gives one control per number, not because rollers are good. Accumulating per event drifts and makes the gesture irreversible; a card mid-fold takes the new value without queueing another animation; the card keeps CLICKABLE and must not go through decor(). Drag faster fixes range and worsens aim, so three gestures share one card.
